source_arguments.statement:
theorem routeETernaryHistoryCoefficient_eq_moebiusProducts
    {Q : Finset Nat.Primes} (h : RouteETernaryHistory Q) :
    routeETernaryHistoryCoefficient h =
      (((μ (routeETernaryLeftProduct h) : ℤ) : ℂ)) *
        (((μ (routeETernaryRightProduct h) : ℤ) : ℂ))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem routeETernaryHistoryCoefficient_eq_moebiusProducts
    {Q : Finset Nat.Primes} (h : RouteETernaryHistory Q) :
    routeETernaryHistoryCoefficient h =
      (((μ (routeETernaryLeftProduct h) : ℤ) : ℂ)) *
        (((μ (routeETernaryRightProduct h) : ℤ) : ℂ))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hmuL := RHTower.GibbsGas.moebius_prod_primes
    (routeETernaryLeftSupport_prime h)
  have hmuR := RHTower.GibbsGas.moebius_prod_primes
    (routeETernaryRightSupport_prime h)
  rw [← routeETernaryLeftProduct_eq_supportProduct] at hmuL
  rw [← routeETernaryRightProduct_eq_supportProduct] at hmuR
  have hmuLC : (((μ (routeETernaryLeftProduct h) : ℤ) : ℂ)) =
      (-1 : ℂ) ^ (routeETernaryLeftSupport h).card := by
    exact_mod_cast hmuL
  have hmuRC : (((μ (routeETernaryRightProduct h) : ℤ) : ℂ)) =
      (-1 : ℂ) ^ (routeETernaryRightSupport h).card := by
    exact_mod_cast hmuR
  rw [hmuLC, hmuRC, routeETernaryHistoryCoefficient]
  simp_rw [routeETernaryLocalCoefficient_split]
  rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib]
  simp [routeETernaryLeftSupport, routeETernaryRightSupport,
    Finset.prod_ite, Finset.card_map]

source_arguments.name: Bottcher.diskPoissonOne_lower_of_blaschke_norm_le
source_arguments.statement:
theorem diskPoissonOne_lower_of_blaschke_norm_le {a w : ℂ} {q : ℝ}
    (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q < 1)
    (hδq : ‖(w - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * w)‖ ≤ q) :
    ((1 - q) / (1 + q)) * diskPoissonOne a ≤ diskPoissonOne w
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem diskPoissonOne_lower_of_blaschke_norm_le {a w : ℂ} {q : ℝ}
    (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q < 1)
    (hδq : ‖(w - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * w)‖ ≤ q) :
    ((1 - q) / (1 + q)) * diskPoissonOne a ≤ diskPoissonOne w
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let η : ℂ := (w - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * w)
  have hden : 1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * w ≠ 0 :=
    one_sub_conj_mul_ne_zero_of_norm_lt_one_norm_le_one ha hw
  have hlower := diskPoissonOne_mobius_lower_of_norm_le (a := a) (η := η) (q := q)
    ha hq0 hq1 (by simpa [η] using hδq)
  have hmob : (a + η) / (1 + (starRingEnd ℂ) a * η) = w := by
    simpa [η] using mobius_of_blaschke (a := a) (w := w) ha hden
  rwa [hmob] at hlower

theorem schwarzian_mobiusObservable (hconst : ∀ t : C, t′ = 0) (x : E)
    (hx : HypertranscendentalOver C x) (a b c d : C) (hdet : a * d - b * c ≠ 0) :

source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem schwarzian_mobiusObservable (hconst : ∀ t : C, t′ = 0) (x : E)
    (hx : HypertranscendentalOver C x) (a b c d : C) (hdet : a * d - b * c ≠ 0) :
    schwarzian (mobiusObservable a b c d x) = schwarzian x
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hden : algebraMap C E c * x + algebraMap C E d ≠ 0 :=
    mobiusDenominator_ne_zero_of_hypertranscendentalOver x hx a b c d hdet
  have hdx : x′ ≠ 0 := deriv_ne_zero_of_hypertranscendentalOver hx
  have hdetE :
      algebraMap C E a * algebraMap C E d - algebraMap C E b * algebraMap C E c ≠ 0 := by
    rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul, ← map_sub]
    simpa using (algebraMap C E).injective.ne hdet
  exact schwarzian_mobius x _ _ _ _ (deriv_algebraMap_eq_zero hconst a)
    (deriv_algebraMap_eq_zero hconst b) (deriv_algebraMap_eq_zero hconst c)
    (deriv_algebraMap_eq_zero hconst d) hdetE hden hdx

theorem tsum_incidenceUpper {ω δ : ℝ} (hω : 0 < ω) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  set N : ℕ := ⌊Real.exp t⌋₊ with hN
  have hsum := (summable_incidenceUpper (δ := δ) hω t).sum_add_tsum_nat_add N
  have hhead : ∑ d ∈ Finset.range N, incidenceUpper ω δ t d = 0 := by
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun d hd => ?_
    rw [Finset.mem_range] at hd
    rw [incidenceUpper_eq ht d, if_pos (by omega)]
  rw [hhead, zero_add] at hsum
  rw [← hsum, mobiusShiftTail, ← tsum_mul_left]
  refine tsum_congr fun i => ?_
  rw [incidenceUpper_eq ht (i + N), if_neg (by omega)]
  have hcast : ((i + N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((i + (N + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) := rfl
  have hcast2 : moebius (i + N + 1) = moebius (i + (N + 1)) := rfl
  rw [hcast, hcast2]

source_arguments.statement:
theorem DifferentialAlgEquiv.not_unit_eigenvector_and_translate_one_on_generators
    (sigma : DifferentialAlgEquiv C T)
    (q r : T) (hq : HypertranscendentalOver C q)
    (hr : HypertranscendentalOver C r)
    (hqgen : differentialAdjoin C ({q} : Set T) = ⊤)
    (hrgen : differentialAdjoin C ({r} : Set T) = ⊤)
    (lam : Cˣ)
    (hqaction : sigma.toAlgEquiv q = q * algebraMap C T (lam : C))
    (hraction : sigma.toAlgEquiv r = r + algebraMap C T 1) : False
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem DifferentialAlgEquiv.not_unit_eigenvector_and_translate_one_on_generators
    (sigma : DifferentialAlgEquiv C T)
    (q r : T) (hq : HypertranscendentalOver C q)
    (hr : HypertranscendentalOver C r)
    (hqgen : differentialAdjoin C ({q} : Set T) = ⊤)
    (hrgen : differentialAdjoin C ({r} : Set T) = ⊤)
    (lam : Cˣ)
    (hqaction : sigma.toAlgEquiv q = q * algebraMap C T (lam : C))
    (hraction : sigma.toAlgEquiv r = r + algebraMap C T 1) : False
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hqr : q ∈ differentialAdjoin C ({r} : Set T) := by
    rw [hrgen]
    trivial
  have hrq : r ∈ differentialAdjoin C ({q} : Set T) := by
    rw [hqgen]
    trivial
  obtain ⟨A, B, c, d, hdet, hmob⟩ := mutual_generator_mobius hq hr hrq hqr
  let AT : T := algebraMap C T A
  let BT : T := algebraMap C T B
  let cT : T := algebraMap C T c
  let dT : T := algebraMap C T d
  let lamT : T := algebraMap C T (lam : C)
  have hmobT : r * (cT * q + dT) = AT * q + BT := by
    simpa [AT, BT, cT, dT] using hmob
  have hmobSigma :
      (r + 1) * (cT * (q * lamT) + dT) = AT * (q * lamT) + BT := by
    have hs := congrArg sigma.toAlgEquiv hmobT
    simpa [AT, BT, cT, dT, lamT, hqaction, hraction, map_add, map_mul,
      sigma.toAlgEquiv.commutes] using hs
  let D0 : T := cT * q + dT
  let D1 : T := cT * (q * lamT) + dT
  let N0 : T := AT * q + BT
  let N1 : T := AT * (q * lamT) + BT
  have hmob0 : r * D0 = N0 := by simpa [D0, N0] using hmobT
  have hmob1 : (r + 1) * D1 = N1 := by simpa [D1, N1] using hmobSigma
  have hshift0 : (r + 1) * D0 = N0 + D0 := by
    calc
      (r + 1) * D0 = r * D0 + D0 := by ring
      _ = N0 + D0 := by rw [hmob0]
  have hclear : (N0 + D0) * D1 - N1 * D0 = 0 := by
    calc
      (N0 + D0) * D1 - N1 * D0 = ((r + 1) * D0) * D1 - N1 * D0 := by
        rw [hshift0]
      _ = ((r + 1) * D1) * D0 - N1 * D0 := by ring
      _ = N1 * D0 - N1 * D0 := by rw [hmob1]
      _ = 0 := sub_self _
  let P : C[X] :=
    Polynomial.monomial 2 (c * c * (lam : C)) +
      Polynomial.monomial 1 ((1 - (lam : C)) * (A * d - B * c) +
        c * d * (1 + (lam : C))) +
      Polynomial.C (d * d)
  have hPeval : Polynomial.aeval q P = 0 := by
    have hexpand : Polynomial.aeval q P = (N0 + D0) * D1 - N1 * D0 := by
      simp [P, N0, N1, D0, D1, AT, BT, cT, dT, lamT]
      ring
    rw [hexpand]
    exact hclear
  have hqtrans : Transcendental C q := by
    simpa using hypertranscendentalOver_jet_transcendental hq 0
  have hPzero : P = 0 := by
    by_contra hP
    exact hqtrans ⟨P, hP, hPeval⟩
  have hd2 : d * d = 0 := by
    have hcoeff := congrArg (fun Q : C[X] => Q.coeff 0) hPzero
    simpa [P, Polynomial.coeff_monomial] using hcoeff
  have hd : d = 0 := (mul_self_eq_zero.mp hd2)
  have hc : c = 0 := by
    have hcoeff := congrArg (fun Q : C[X] => Q.coeff 2) hPzero
    simpa [P, hd, Polynomial.coeff_monomial] using hcoeff
  apply hdet
  simp [hc, hd]

method.description: The proof shows that a contradiction arises from the properties of the algebraic action of sigma on q and r, using the mutual generator Mobius transformation and evaluating a polynomial at q.
steps: apply sigma to the Mobius equation
evaluate polynomial at q and derive contradiction
obligations: use determinant condition to conclude False
evidence: obtain ⟨A, B, c, d, hdet, hmob⟩ := mutual_generator_mobius hq hr hrq hqr
have hPeval : Polynomial.aeval q P = 0 := by

# Connes/CCM RH research handover

Date: 2026-07-25

## Mission and success condition

Resume the Connes–Consani–Moscovici lane, guided by Lean as the authoritative research corpus.
Only one of these is terminal progress:

1. `[LEAN-PROVED]` unconditional
   `P_-(L) ≤ C_Γ(L) + P_+(L)` for every `L ≥ π/2`, hence RH;
2. a concrete proved violating `L`, hence disproof of RH;
3. an unconditional theorem excluding every CCM-admissible infinite source transport.

Do not count equivalent RH criteria, estimates, infrastructure, or another excluded subclass.
Use `hgt-fields-medalist`; read `docs/meta/scientific-method.md` and failed-route cards first.

## Exact endpoint already closed in Lean

For finite right-half-plane nodes `P`, the required object is

```text
W_P = [[G_P, r_P], [r_Pᴴ, 4]],
r_P(i) = continuedXiAntiCausalWardResponse(P_i).
```

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/GammaSewnMobiusXiWardCofinalBoundaryLift.lean` proves:

- `continuedXiWardFourUnitBoundaryGram_posSemidef_iff_schur`;
- `riemannHypothesis_iff_continuedXiWardFourUnitBoundaryLiftLaw`;
- the equivalent boundary-Gram law;
- under `¬RH`, one zero-adapted one-node packet makes the Schur defect strictly negative.

Thus unconditional source-side positivity of every `W_P` is exactly RH, not an auxiliary lemma.
`XiWardThresholdEightClosedCompleteness.lean` also closes the two-sided threshold-eight endpoint.

## Exact source geometry already closed

- `MobiusCriticalFisherLowerBoundaryBudget.lean`: actual one-sided lower-corner Hilbert–Schmidt
  energy has critical total `4`.
- `RankTwoFisherCutoffWard.lean`: pointed Fisher connection is the canonical rank-two operator
  `2⁻¹/²(|χ><ψ|+|ψ><χ|)`; its cutoff corners are explicit.
- `EulerSquarefreeDyadicAffineProjection.lean`: exact unitary reindexing `n = d m²`, preserving
  cutoff corners and Hilbert–Schmidt energy.
- `EulerSquarefreeAffineFisherCutoffWard.lean`: the full positive Euler source retains the same
  critical four-unit Fisher/Ward law.
- `FisherOneCornerCoareaTransform.lean` and
  `InfiniteFisherOneCornerCodiagonalContraction.lean`: universal one-corner contraction machinery.
- `SoninBurnolPointedWardTrace.lean`: hypothesis-free Lüders/Burnol boundary split.
- `SoninCofinalMobiusGammaXiIncidence.lean`: source-defined noncompact/cofinal Sonin transports
  reconstruct the full continued Xi trace on the Euler region. Energy incidence is not proved.
- `EulerAffineGammaXiWardTransport.lean`: exact singular graph transport from the all-Euler Fisher
  numerator to the continued Xi source.
- `SquarefreeFixedCurrentLocalization.lean`: division-free identity

```text
ε B_σ(u) J_sq(σ+uε) = -∂_u B_σ(u),
B_σ(u)=squarefreePartition(σ+uε)/squarefreePartition(σ).
```

The strict-right Xi divisor is exactly the failure set of the continued multiplication quotient.

## Paper-proved source completion

Read:

- `docs/drafts/pipeline/2-fully-proven/gamma-sonin-asymptotic-passivity-incidence-curvature.md`;
- `.../complementary-packet-euler-connection-weld.md`;
- `.../complementary-packet-critical-gini-isometry.md`;
- `.../mobius-fixed-current-von-mangoldt-critical-transport-weld.md`;
- `.../mobius-causal-fisher-connection-flatness.md`.

They establish on paper:

- entrywise Gamma completion is asymptotically passive;
- Sonin projection is contractive;
- complementary packets and Euler fixed-current transport preserve the four-unit cofinal budget;
- the assembled causal derivative is Fisher-flat: its two connection terms cancel before the
  Gamma/Sonin boundary split.

Verify exact Lean status before importing any paper-only claim.

## Current open core

Active research card:

`docs/drafts/pipeline/1-in-progress/mobius-incidence-curvature-gamma-sonin-pole-divisor-transfer-rh.md`

`[OPEN CORE]` Construct, before any Xi divisor or target Gram is named, the charged anti-causal
codifferential of the completed Euler-current edge field on the closed multiplication graph
`Graph(B_σ)`. Prove all three:

1. the completed Fisher numerator lies in the source-selected graph range;
2. its anti-causal graph quotient/curvature is exactly the squarefree Hardy block, hence tends to
   `r_P`;
3. Gauss–Codazzi gives a nonnegative causal remainder:

```text
source four-unit curvature
  = anti-causal curvature energy + causal remainder energy.
```

This would give `‖r_P‖²_{G_P⁻¹} ≤ 4`, hence `W_P ⪰ 0`, hence RH.

Equivalent pointwise slogan `|r(1/2+it)| ≤ 2` is not enough unless derived from this source object.

## Anti-theatre results already settled

- `[REDISCOVERED/CIRCULAR]` Orthogonal Hardy projection of the continued logarithmic derivative is

- `[CORPUS]` `GammaSewnMobiusXiWardHardyTransport.lean` constructs a target-side Julia transport
  whose derivative is `r`; `GammaSewnMobiusXiWardHardyContraction.lean` bounds the finite transport

## Lean formalization

`LandauIntegralTransfer.lean` proves the reusable continuous Taylor--Tonelli theorem for a
nonnegative random variable: analytic continuation of its complex MGF through a closed ball
forces every positive exponential moment strictly inside that ball.

`MobiusLaplaceLandauOscillation.lean` then formalizes the complete source specialization:

- unconditional sharp geometric estimate `||Phi(x)|| <= 1/x` and classical Mellin convergence;
- exact power-comparison Mellin identity and entire cutoff-tail transform;

All target modules compile with `lake env lean`; no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `opaque`, or
`unsafe` declaration is introduced.  Remaining open endpoint is still exact exponent `1/2`.

The half-power exponent is a genuine zero-edge oscillation barrier from below: every weaker power
normalization fails by unbounded positive and negative excursions.  Any viable proof of the open
upper bound must therefore control an intrinsically cofinal oscillatory source; eventual
positivity, monotonicity, finite sign charts, and subcritical absolute majorants are impossible.
The remaining open core is exactly sharp upper cancellation at exponent `1/2`, or equivalently
the already formalized Mellin continuation wall.

import Mathlib

/-!
# Weyl-algebra source for the negative local-Fourier branch

This module constructs the first Weyl algebra over `ℂ` from its presentation, rather than
postulating exponent transitions.  It supplies four independent pieces of source semantics:

* free noncommutative operator words evaluated by multiplication and differentiation on `ℂ[X]`;
* the two-sided Weyl relation `D X - X D = 1` and its quotient algebra;
* the algebraic Fourier automorphism `X ↦ D`, `D ↦ -X`, including its order-four law;
* polynomial gauge/addition automorphisms `D ↦ D + p(X)`.

The final section proves the exact monomial curve contact chart used by Hiroe's
`F^(∞,∞)` transform.  For an Airy step `β = R + E`, the transformed coordinate has order `E`
and the old leading exponent `β` is divisible by `E`.  This is the genuine leading-edge source
of the negative rank drop.  Preservation of a general lower characteristic tail is intentionally
not asserted here.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions
namespace IrregularStokes
namespace WeylFourier

noncomputable section

/-! ## Presented operators and their polynomial semantics -/

/-- Coordinate and derivative generators of the first Weyl algebra. -/
inductive Generator
  | coordinate
  | derivative
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- Free noncommutative operator words before imposing the Weyl commutator. -/
abbrev PresentedWeyl := FreeAlgebra ℂ Generator

/-- Coordinate generator in the free presentation. -/
def coordinateWord : PresentedWeyl := FreeAlgebra.ι ℂ Generator.coordinate

/-- Derivative generator in the free presentation. -/
def derivativeWord : PresentedWeyl := FreeAlgebra.ι ℂ Generator.derivative

/-- Multiplication by `X` on the polynomial representation. -/
def polynomialCoordinateOperator : Module.End ℂ (Polynomial ℂ) :=
  LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ Polynomial.X

/-- Polynomial differentiation on the polynomial representation. -/
def polynomialDerivativeOperator : Module.End ℂ (Polynomial ℂ) :=
  Polynomial.derivative

/-- Actual action of presented operator words on complex polynomials. -/
def operatorSemantics :
    PresentedWeyl →ₐ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ (Polynomial ℂ) :=
  FreeAlgebra.lift ℂ (fun
    | Generator.coordinate => polynomialCoordinateOperator
    | Generator.derivative => polynomialDerivativeOperator)

/-- Multiplication and differentiation satisfy the Weyl commutator on every polynomial. -/
theorem operatorSemantics_commutator :
    operatorSemantics
        (derivativeWord * coordinateWord - coordinateWord * derivativeWord) = 1 := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro p
  simp only [map_sub, map_mul]
  simp only [operatorSemantics, derivativeWord, coordinateWord,
    FreeAlgebra.lift_ι_apply]
  change Polynomial.derivative (Polynomial.X * p) -
    Polynomial.X * Polynomial.derivative p = p
  rw [Polynomial.derivative_mul, Polynomial.derivative_X]
  simp

/-! ## Algebraic Fourier transform on the presentation -/

/-- Forward algebraic Fourier substitution `X ↦ D`, `D ↦ -X`. -/
def fourierWordHom : PresentedWeyl →ₐ[ℂ] PresentedWeyl :=
  FreeAlgebra.lift ℂ (fun
    | Generator.coordinate => derivativeWord
    | Generator.derivative => -coordinateWord)

/-- Inverse algebraic Fourier substitution `X ↦ -D`, `D ↦ X`. -/
def inverseFourierWordHom : PresentedWeyl →ₐ[ℂ] PresentedWeyl :=
  FreeAlgebra.lift ℂ (fun
    | Generator.coordinate => -derivativeWord
    | Generator.derivative => coordinateWord)

theorem fourierWordHom_inverseFourierWordHom :
    fourierWordHom.comp inverseFourierWordHom = AlgHom.id ℂ PresentedWeyl := by
  apply FreeAlgebra.hom_ext
  funext g
  cases g <;> simp [fourierWordHom, inverseFourierWordHom,
    coordinateWord, derivativeWord]

theorem inverseFourierWordHom_fourierWordHom :
    inverseFourierWordHom.comp fourierWordHom = AlgHom.id ℂ PresentedWeyl := by
  apply FreeAlgebra.hom_ext
  funext g
  cases g <;> simp [fourierWordHom, inverseFourierWordHom,
    coordinateWord, derivativeWord]

/-- Algebraic Fourier transform as an actual automorphism of presented operators. -/
def fourierWord : PresentedWeyl ≃ₐ[ℂ] PresentedWeyl :=
  AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom fourierWordHom inverseFourierWordHom
    fourierWordHom_inverseFourierWordHom inverseFourierWordHom_fourierWordHom

@[simp] theorem fourierWord_coordinate :
    fourierWord coordinateWord = derivativeWord := by
  simp [fourierWord, fourierWordHom, coordinateWord, derivativeWord]

@[simp] theorem fourierWord_derivative :
    fourierWord derivativeWord = -coordinateWord := by
  simp [fourierWord, fourierWordHom, coordinateWord, derivativeWord]

/-- Relation whose vanishing presents the first Weyl algebra. -/
def weylRelation : PresentedWeyl :=
  derivativeWord * coordinateWord - coordinateWord * derivativeWord - 1

/-- Fourier substitution preserves the Weyl relation exactly. -/
theorem fourierWord_weylRelation : fourierWord weylRelation = weylRelation := by
  simp [weylRelation]
  noncomm_ring

/-- Algebraic Fourier transform has order four on every presented operator. -/

/-!
# The terminal multiplier is not constant in its own coordinate

The multiplier of a coordinate jet contains, at the newest coordinate, the rational function

`W = Q'·v/Q + α·Q`.

It is constant in that coordinate exactly when the polynomial Wronskian `N'·Q − N·Q'` vanishes, where
`N = Q'·v + α·Q²` is the cleared numerator.  Expanding,

`N'·Q − N·Q' = α·Q²·Q' + ((Q'v)'·Q − (Q')²·v)`,

and for `deg Q ≥ 1` and linear `v` the first term has degree `3·deg Q − 1` while the rest has degree at
most `2·deg Q − 1`.  So the Wronskian is nonzero, and the multiplier genuinely depends on its own
coordinate — the diagonal entry of the height induction.

The exponential tower is the degenerate-looking case `Q = v = X`, where the Wronskian is `α·X²` — the
statement is sharp: for constant `Q` the multiplier really is independent of the coordinate.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Polynomial

/-- The cleared numerator of the terminal multiplier. -/
noncomputable def terminalNumer (Q v : Polynomial ℂ) (α : ℂ) : Polynomial ℂ :=
  Q.derivative * v + Polynomial.C α * Q ^ 2

/-- The Wronskian of the numerator against the denominator. -/
noncomputable def terminalWronskian (Q v : Polynomial ℂ) (α : ℂ) : Polynomial ℂ :=
  (terminalNumer Q v α).derivative * Q - terminalNumer Q v α * Q.derivative

theorem terminalWronskian_expand (Q v : Polynomial ℂ) (α : ℂ) :
    terminalWronskian Q v α
      = Polynomial.C α * (Q ^ 2 * Q.derivative)
        + ((Q.derivative * v).derivative * Q - Q.derivative ^ 2 * v) := by
  rw [terminalWronskian, terminalNumer]
  simp only [derivative_add, derivative_mul, derivative_C, derivative_pow, zero_mul, zero_add,
    Nat.cast_ofNat, map_ofNat]
  ring

/-- **The terminal multiplier is nonconstant in its coordinate.**  For a nonconstant `Q`, a linear
`v` and a nonzero slope, the Wronskian does not vanish. -/
theorem terminalWronskian_ne_zero {Q v : Polynomial ℂ} {α : ℂ}
    (hα : α ≠ 0) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q.natDegree) (hv : v.natDegree ≤ 1) :
    terminalWronskian Q v α ≠ 0 := by
  have hQ0 : Q ≠ 0 := fun h => by simp [h] at hQ
  have hmain : (Polynomial.C α * (Q ^ 2 * Q.derivative)).degree
      = ((3 * Q.natDegree - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := by
    rw [Polynomial.degree_mul, Polynomial.degree_C hα, zero_add, Polynomial.degree_mul,
      Polynomial.degree_pow, Polynomial.degree_derivative (p := Q) (by omega),
      Polynomial.degree_eq_natDegree hQ0]
    have h2 : (2 : ℕ) • (Q.natDegree : WithBot ℕ) = ((2 * Q.natDegree : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := by
      push_cast
      ring
    rw [h2, ← Nat.cast_add]
    congr 1
    omega
  have hrestnat : ((Q.derivative * v).derivative * Q - Q.derivative ^ 2 * v).natDegree
      ≤ 2 * Q.natDegree - 1 := by
    refine le_trans (Polynomial.natDegree_sub_le _ _) (max_le ?_ ?_)
    · refine le_trans (Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le) ?_
      have h1 : (Q.derivative * v).derivative.natDegree ≤ Q.natDegree - 1 := by
        refine le_trans (Polynomial.natDegree_derivative_le _) ?_
        have h2 : (Q.derivative * v).natDegree ≤ Q.natDegree := by
          refine le_trans (Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le) ?_
          have := Polynomial.natDegree_derivative_le Q
          omega
        omega
      omega
    · refine le_trans (Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le) ?_
      have h3 : (Q.derivative ^ 2).natDegree ≤ 2 * (Q.natDegree - 1) := by
        refine le_trans (Polynomial.natDegree_pow_le) ?_
        have := Polynomial.natDegree_derivative_le Q
        omega
      omega
  have hrest : ((Q.derivative * v).derivative * Q - Q.derivative ^ 2 * v).degree
      ≤ ((2 * Q.natDegree - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) :=
    Polynomial.natDegree_le_iff_degree_le.mp hrestnat
  have hlt : ((2 * Q.natDegree - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ)
      < ((3 * Q.natDegree - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := by
    exact_mod_cast Nat.cast_lt.mpr (by omega : 2 * Q.natDegree - 1 < 3 * Q.natDegree - 1)
  rw [terminalWronskian_expand]
  intro h0
  have hdeg := Polynomial.degree_add_eq_left_of_degree_lt
    (p := Polynomial.C α * (Q ^ 2 * Q.derivative))
    (q := (Q.derivative * v).derivative * Q - Q.derivative ^ 2 * v)
    (by rw [hmain]; exact lt_of_le_of_lt hrest hlt)
  rw [h0, Polynomial.degree_zero, hmain] at hdeg
  exact absurd hdeg.symm (by simp)

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# W-coordinate PT first-jet covariance universality law

The Li/Bombieri--Lagarias coordinate conjugates the functional-equation involution
`sigma(z) = 1 - z` to inversion.  The scalar conjugacy extends to an exact first-jet law:
the reflected derivative is transported by the product of the Li-coordinate Jacobian and the
inversion Jacobian.  This holds for every scalar function differentiable at the transported point.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- The Li coordinate has inverse-square derivative away from its pole. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_wCoordinate {z : ℂ} (hz : z ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt wCoordinate (z⁻¹ ^ 2) z := by
  unfold wCoordinate
  simpa [inv_pow] using!
    (hasDerivAt_const (x := z) (c := (1 : ℂ))).sub (hasDerivAt_inv hz)

/-- The derivative weight at the reflected point factors into the Li-coordinate Jacobian and
the inversion Jacobian. -/
theorem wCoordinate_PT_derivativeWeight
    {z : ℂ} (hz0 : z ≠ 0) :
    (sigma z)⁻¹ ^ 2 = z⁻¹ ^ 2 * (wCoordinate z)⁻¹ ^ 2 := by
  unfold sigma wCoordinate
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **W-coordinate PT first-jet covariance universality law.**  Away from `0` and `1`, functional-
equation pullback of `f ∘ w` is inversion pullback in the `w` coordinate.  Its first derivative
acquires exactly the product of the `w`-Jacobian `z⁻²` and inversion weight `w(z)⁻²`, together with
the PT sign. -/
theorem wCoordinate_fePullback_firstJet
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) {z f' : ℂ} (hz0 : z ≠ 0) (hz1 : z ≠ 1)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f f' ((wCoordinate z)⁻¹)) :
    fePullback (fun s => f (wCoordinate s)) z =
        f ((wCoordinate z)⁻¹) ∧
      HasDerivAt (fePullback (fun s => f (wCoordinate s)))
        (-(f' * z⁻¹ ^ 2 * (wCoordinate z)⁻¹ ^ 2)) z := by
  have hsigma0 : sigma z ≠ 0 := by
    unfold sigma
    exact sub_ne_zero.mpr hz1.symm
  have hcoord : wCoordinate (sigma z) = (wCoordinate z)⁻¹ :=
    wCoordinate_sigma_eq_inv z hz0 hz1
  have hinner : HasDerivAt (fun s => f (wCoordinate s))
      (f' * (sigma z)⁻¹ ^ 2) (sigma z) := by
    exact (hcoord ▸ hf).comp (sigma z) (hasDerivAt_wCoordinate hsigma0)
  refine ⟨by simp only [fePullback_apply, hcoord], ?_⟩
  have hpull := hasDerivAt_fePullback hinner
  rw [wCoordinate_PT_derivativeWeight hz0] at hpull
  simpa only [mul_assoc] using hpull

end

end GaloisForLFunctions

/-!
# Irreducible derivative polynomial over the rational state field

The irreducible analytic Wiman relation remains irreducible after singling out the derivative
coordinate and passing from the polynomial state ring to its fraction field.  This is the exact
component-uniqueness bridge required before a prescribed Newton place can be transported to the
actual derivative field.
-/

noncomputable section

/-- The two indices left after removing the derivative coordinate. -/
noncomputable def firstOrderStateIndexEquiv :
    {j : Fin 3 // j ≠ (2 : Fin 3)} ≃ Fin 2 :=
  Equiv.ofBijective
    (fun j => (⟨j.1.val, by omega⟩ : Fin 2))
    ⟨fun i j hij => by
        apply Subtype.ext
        apply Fin.ext
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin 2 => x.val) hij
        exact hval,
      fun j => by
        let i : Fin 3 := ⟨j.val, by omega⟩
        have hi : i ≠ (2 : Fin 3) := by
          intro h
          have := congrArg Fin.val h
          change j.val = 2 at this
          omega
        exact ⟨⟨i, hi⟩, Fin.ext rfl⟩⟩

/-- Literal iterated polynomial ring `ℂ[U][V]` for the clock and value coordinates. -/
abbrev FirstOrderStatePolynomialRing := Polynomial (Polynomial ℂ)

/-- The remaining-coordinate multivariable ring is exactly the iterated state polynomial ring. -/
noncomputable def firstOrderStatePolynomialEquiv :
    MvPolynomial {j : Fin 3 // j ≠ (2 : Fin 3)} ℂ ≃ₐ[ℂ]
      FirstOrderStatePolynomialRing :=
  (MvPolynomial.renameEquiv ℂ firstOrderStateIndexEquiv).trans
    ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℂ 1).trans
      (Polynomial.mapAlgEquiv
        ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℂ 0).trans
          (Polynomial.mapAlgEquiv (MvPolynomial.isEmptyAlgEquiv ℂ (Fin 0))))))

/-- Rational function field in the clock and value coordinates. -/
abbrev FirstOrderRationalStateField := FractionRing FirstOrderStatePolynomialRing

/-- A three-variable relation viewed literally as a polynomial in the derivative coordinate. -/
noncomputable def firstOrderDerivativePolynomialOverStateRing
    (P : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ) : Polynomial FirstOrderStatePolynomialRing :=
  (mvPolynomialPolynomialEquivAt (2 : Fin 3) P).map
    firstOrderStatePolynomialEquiv.toRingHom

/-- The derivative polynomial after passing to the rational clock/value state field. -/
noncomputable def firstOrderDerivativePolynomial
    (P : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℂ) : Polynomial FirstOrderRationalStateField :=
  (firstOrderDerivativePolynomialOverStateRing P).map
    (algebraMap FirstOrderStatePolynomialRing FirstOrderRationalStateField)

/-- Vanishing of the coordinate derivative gives the reduced numerator-denominator Wronskian
identity. -/
theorem ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_eq_zero_cross
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (z : RatFunc K)
    (hz : ratFuncCoordinateDerivation K z = 0) :
    z.denom * z.num.derivative - z.num * z.denom.derivative = 0 := by
  have hden : algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.denom ≠ 0 :=
    fun hzero => RatFunc.denom_ne_zero z
      (IsFractionRing.injective K[X] (RatFunc K) (by simpa using hzero))
  rw [← RatFunc.num_div_denom z] at hz
  rw [Derivation.leibniz_div,
    ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_algebraMap,
    ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_algebraMap] at hz
  simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hz
  have hcrossF :
      algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.denom *
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.num.derivative -
        algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.num *
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.denom.derivative = 0 :=
    (mul_eq_zero.mp hz).resolve_left (pow_ne_zero 2 (inv_ne_zero hden))
  exact IsFractionRing.injective K[X] (RatFunc K)
    (by simpa only [map_sub, map_mul, map_zero] using hcrossF)

/-- Over a field, a polynomial which divides its own derivative has zero derivative. -/
theorem polynomial_derivative_eq_zero_of_dvd_self
    {K : Type*} [Field K] {p : K[X]} (h : p ∣ p.derivative) :
    p.derivative = 0 := by
  by_contra hp'
  have hdeg : p.natDegree ≠ 0 := by
    intro hpdeg
    exact hp' (Polynomial.derivative_of_natDegree_zero hpdeg)
  exact (not_lt_of_ge (Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd h hp'))
    (Polynomial.natDegree_derivative_lt hdeg)

/-- If a rational coordinate derivative vanishes, its reduced numerator is constant. -/
theorem ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_num_derivative_eq_zero
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (z : RatFunc K)
    (hz : ratFuncCoordinateDerivation K z = 0) :
    z.num.derivative = 0 := by
  have hcross := ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_eq_zero_cross z hz
  have heq : z.denom * z.num.derivative = z.num * z.denom.derivative :=
    sub_eq_zero.mp hcross
  have hdiv : z.num ∣ z.num.derivative * z.denom := by
    refine ⟨z.denom.derivative, ?_⟩
    calc
      z.num.derivative * z.denom = z.denom * z.num.derivative := mul_comm _ _
      _ = z.num * z.denom.derivative := heq
  exact polynomial_derivative_eq_zero_of_dvd_self
    ((RatFunc.isCoprime_num_denom z).dvd_of_dvd_mul_right hdiv)

/-- If a rational coordinate derivative vanishes, its normalized denominator is constant. -/
theorem ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_denom_derivative_eq_zero
    {K : Type*} [Field K] (z : RatFunc K)
    (hz : ratFuncCoordinateDerivation K z = 0) :
    z.denom.derivative = 0 := by
  have hcross := ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_eq_zero_cross z hz
  have heq : z.denom * z.num.derivative = z.num * z.denom.derivative :=
    sub_eq_zero.mp hcross
  have hdiv : z.denom ∣ z.denom.derivative * z.num := by
    refine ⟨z.num.derivative, ?_⟩
    calc
      z.denom.derivative * z.num = z.num * z.denom.derivative := mul_comm _ _
      _ = z.denom * z.num.derivative := heq.symm
  exact polynomial_derivative_eq_zero_of_dvd_self
    ((RatFunc.isCoprime_num_denom z).symm.dvd_of_dvd_mul_right hdiv)

/-- **Rational coordinate rigidity.**  In characteristic zero the constants of the coordinate
derivation on `K(t)` are exactly the coefficient field `K`. -/
theorem ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_eq_zero_iff
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] (z : RatFunc K) :
    ratFuncCoordinateDerivation K z = 0 ↔
      ∃ c : K, z = algebraMap K (RatFunc K) c := by
  constructor
  · intro hz
    have hp : z.num = Polynomial.C (z.num.coeff 0) :=
      Polynomial.eq_C_of_derivative_eq_zero
        (ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_num_derivative_eq_zero z hz)
    have hq : z.denom = Polynomial.C (z.denom.coeff 0) :=
      Polynomial.eq_C_of_derivative_eq_zero
        (ratFuncCoordinateDerivation_denom_derivative_eq_zero z hz)
    let a := z.num.coeff 0
    let b := z.denom.coeff 0
    refine ⟨a / b, ?_⟩
    calc
      z = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.num /
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) z.denom :=
        (RatFunc.num_div_denom z).symm
      _ = algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (Polynomial.C a) /
          algebraMap K[X] (RatFunc K) (Polynomial.C b) := by
        rw [hp, hq]
      _ = algebraMap K (RatFunc K) a / algebraMap K (RatFunc K) b := by
        congr 1
      _ = algebraMap K (RatFunc K) (a / b) :=
        (map_div₀ (algebraMap K (RatFunc K)) a b).symm
  · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
    exact Derivation.map_algebraMap _ _

end

/-!
# Exposed normal-summability connectors for Poincare series

Positive-factor construction already proves normal convergence through bundled
`GaussianFlatIntegerLatticeSeedsNormallySummable` interface. This module exposes its strongest
direct mathlib-shaped consequence: one Gaussian scale works simultaneously for every target and
every polynomial multiplier in finite interpolation packet.
-/

open Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- **Uniform Gaussian Poincare summability law.** An Abe-positive presentation supplies one
positive Gaussian scale at which every explicit flat-separator seed in packet is locally normally
summable, uniformly over chosen target and polynomial multiplier. -/
theorem AbePositiveFactorPresentation.exists_gaussianScale_summableLocallyUniformlyOn
    {d : ℕ} (P : AbePositiveFactorPresentation.{u} d)
    (I : Type u) [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (w : I → Fin d → ℂ)
    (hdistinct : PairwiseDistinctModulo (standardIntegerLattice d) w)
    (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :
    ∃ σ : Fin d → ℝ, (∀ c, 0 < σ c) ∧
      ∀ (target : I) (Q : MvPolynomial (Fin d) ℂ),
        let S := flatIntegerLatticePacketSeparatorData w hdistinct target m hm
        let D := gaussianFlatSeedData σ (w target) hm
        SummableLocallyUniformlyOn
          (fun γ ↦ poincareTerm P.factor
            (multivariateEntireMul S.bump
              (multivariateEntireMul D.damping
                (mvPolynomialMultivariateEntire Q))) γ)
          Set.univ := by
  exact P.gaussianFlatSeedsNormallySummable I w hdistinct m hm

end

/-!
# Summability under uniformly positive reweighting

A nonnegative real family remains summable, and only remains summable, after multiplication by a
weight bounded above and bounded away from zero.  This is the common comparison interface behind
the fixed, tangent, and cubic source/value reflection apertures in `RHTower`.
-/

namespace HTGeometry

/-- Multiplication by a uniformly bounded positive weight preserves and reflects summability of a
nonnegative real family.  The index type is arbitrary, and the upper bound needs no separate sign
hypothesis. -/
theorem summable_mul_iff_of_nonneg_of_uniform_pos_le_of_le
    {ι : Type*} (f w : ι → ℝ) {c C : ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hlower : ∀ i, c ≤ w i) (hupper : ∀ i, w i ≤ C) :
    Summable (fun i => w i * f i) ↔ Summable f := by
  constructor
  · intro hweighted
    have hscaled : Summable (fun i => c * f i) := by
      exact Summable.of_nonneg_of_le
        (fun i => mul_nonneg hc.le (hf i))
        (fun i => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hlower i) (hf i))
        hweighted
    exact (summable_mul_left_iff hc.ne').mp hscaled
  · intro hbase
    have hmajor : Summable (fun i => C * f i) := hbase.mul_left C
    exact Summable.of_nonneg_of_le
      (fun i => mul_nonneg (le_trans hc.le (hlower i)) (hf i))
      (fun i => mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hupper i) (hf i))
      hmajor

end HTGeometry

/-!
# All-place Green-form uniform-packet no-go

Operator-norm summability of local Green forms on one defining Banach disk forces their norms to
vanish.  Hence one disk cannot contain unit-norm packets whose own-place Green diagonal remains
one.  Applied to Route L, graph-normalized high-prime packets must escape every fixed source disk
or acquire arithmetic damping before the all-place form sum can converge.

This is unconditional functional analysis.  It uses no Xi zero, spectral projector, numerical
computation, or RH premise.
-/

namespace RHTower

open Filter Topology

open scoped BigOperators

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

/-- Norm summability forces the norms of the summands to vanish. -/
theorem deningerSummableTerm_norm_tendsto_zero
    {A : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup A]
    (f : ℕ → A) (hf : Summable f) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ‖f n‖) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  have hzero : Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0) := hf.tendsto_atTop_zero
  simpa using hzero.norm

/-- A uniform positive operator-norm floor forbids all-place form summability. -/
theorem deningerGreenForm_not_summable_of_uniform_norm_floor
    (localForm : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hfloor : ∀ n, ε ≤ ‖localForm n‖) :
    ¬ Summable localForm := by
  intro hforms
  have hvanish := deningerSummableTerm_norm_tendsto_zero localForm hforms
  have heventually : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ‖localForm n‖ < ε :=
    hvanish.eventually_lt_const hε
  rcases (eventually_atTop.1 heventually) with ⟨N, hN⟩
  exact (not_lt_of_ge (hfloor N)) (hN N le_rfl)

/-- A unit vector with unit Green diagonal forces the form norm to be at least one. -/
theorem deningerGreenForm_one_le_norm_of_normalized_packet
    (G : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (x : E)
    (hx : ‖x‖ = 1) (henergy : G x x = 1) :
    1 ≤ ‖G‖ := by
  have hinner := (G x).le_opNorm x
  have houter := G.le_opNorm x
  rw [henergy, hx, norm_one, mul_one] at hinner
  rw [hx, mul_one] at houter
  exact hinner.trans houter

/-- Quantitative operator-norm inequality behind normalized-packet escape. -/
theorem deningerGreenForm_one_le_norm_mul_packet_norm_sq
    (G : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) (x : E)
    (henergy : G x x = 1) :
    1 ≤ ‖G‖ * ‖x‖ ^ 2 := by
  have hinner := (G x).le_opNorm x
  have houter := G.le_opNorm x
  calc
    1 = ‖G x x‖ := by rw [henergy, norm_one]
    _ ≤ ‖G x‖ * ‖x‖ := hinner
    _ ≤ (‖G‖ * ‖x‖) * ‖x‖ :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right houter (norm_nonneg x)
    _ = ‖G‖ * ‖x‖ ^ 2 := by ring

/-- Under all-place form summability, unit own-place energy forces packet norms to infinity. -/
theorem deningerGreenForm_normalized_packets_norm_tendsto_atTop
    (localForm : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (packet : ℕ → E)
    (hforms : Summable localForm)
    (hpacket_energy : ∀ n, localForm n (packet n) (packet n) = 1) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ‖packet n‖) atTop atTop := by
  rw [tendsto_atTop_atTop]
  intro b
  let M : ℝ := max b 1
  have hbM : b ≤ M := le_max_left _ _
  have hM : 0 < M := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one (le_max_right _ _)
  have hthreshold : 0 < (M ^ 2)⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr (sq_pos_of_pos hM)
  have hvanish := deningerSummableTerm_norm_tendsto_zero localForm hforms
  have heventually : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ‖localForm n‖ < (M ^ 2)⁻¹ :=
    hvanish.eventually_lt_const hthreshold
  rcases (eventually_atTop.1 heventually) with ⟨N, hN⟩
  refine ⟨N, fun n hn => ?_⟩
  by_contra hnot
  have hxlt : ‖packet n‖ < b := lt_of_not_ge hnot
  have hxle : ‖packet n‖ ≤ M := (le_of_lt hxlt).trans hbM
  have hsq : ‖packet n‖ ^ 2 ≤ M ^ 2 :=
    (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) hM.le).2 hxle
  have hxne : packet n ≠ 0 := by
    intro hx
    simpa [hx] using hpacket_energy n
  have hxnormsq : 0 < ‖packet n‖ ^ 2 :=
    sq_pos_of_pos (norm_pos_iff.mpr hxne)
  have hprodlt :
      ‖localForm n‖ * ‖packet n‖ ^ 2 < (M ^ 2)⁻¹ * M ^ 2 :=
    mul_lt_mul (hN n hn) hsq hxnormsq hthreshold.le
  rw [inv_mul_cancel₀ (pow_ne_zero 2 hM.ne')] at hprodlt
  exact (not_lt_of_ge
    (deningerGreenForm_one_le_norm_mul_packet_norm_sq
      (localForm n) (packet n) (hpacket_energy n))) hprodlt

/-- Unit-norm packets with unit own-place Green energy obstruct all-place form summability. -/
theorem deningerGreenForm_not_summable_of_normalized_packets
    (localForm : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ)
    (packet : ℕ → E)
    (hpacket_norm : ∀ n, ‖packet n‖ = 1)
    (hpacket_energy : ∀ n, localForm n (packet n) (packet n) = 1) :
    ¬ Summable localForm :=
  deningerGreenForm_not_summable_of_uniform_norm_floor
    localForm zero_lt_one fun n =>
      deningerGreenForm_one_le_norm_of_normalized_packet
        (localForm n) (packet n) (hpacket_norm n) (hpacket_energy n)

majorant for the individual operator norms. -/

/-!
# Controlling the accumulated growth

A chain of tunable transfer steps multiplies the kernel bound by `√((1+εₖ)/(1−δₖ))` at each step, so
the bound after `n` steps carries the product `∏ (1 + aₖ)`.  Since `1 + x ≤ exp x`, that product is
at most `exp (∑ aₖ)`, which is bounded uniformly in `n` whenever the parameters are summable.

This is what turns link 132's summability witness into a uniform bound along the chain.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace HTGeometry

/-- **A product of `1 + aₖ` is controlled by the exponential of the sum.** -/
theorem prod_one_add_le_exp_sum (n : ℕ) {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ k, 0 ≤ a k) :
    ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, (1 + a k) ≤ Real.exp (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, a k) := by
  rw [Real.exp_sum]
  refine Finset.prod_le_prod (fun k _ => by linarith [ha k]) fun k _ => ?_
  have h := Real.add_one_le_exp (a k)
  linarith

/-- With summable parameters the bound is uniform in the number of steps. -/
theorem prod_one_add_le_exp_tsum (n : ℕ) {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ k, 0 ≤ a k)
    (hsum : Summable a) :
    ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, (1 + a k) ≤ Real.exp (∑' k, a k) := by
  refine le_trans (prod_one_add_le_exp_sum n ha) ?_
  refine Real.exp_le_exp.mpr ?_
  exact hsum.sum_le_tsum _ fun k _ => ha k

end HTGeometry

/-!
# Uniform cofinal bound for Suzuki's dressed marked halfgap debt

Pointwise summability of the aperture-dressed marked completion does not by itself control a
cofinal Ward residual: its total mass could still grow with observer aperture or spectral height.
The all-prime wall majorant is in fact independent of both variables.  This module exposes the
resulting exact total-mass identity and the uniform ceiling

`total halfgap debt ≤ C(h) * (r - m*s)^2`,

where `C(h)` is one fixed convergent prime-log square sum.  Consequently the marked halfgap
channel cannot make the rectangular Ward residual escape to negative infinity at fixed source
scale.  Remaining RH-bearing work is the source occurrence and Schur comparison of the actual
Robin--Gamma--holonomy trace with the completed negative-light Gram; it is not halfgap
summability or cofinal growth.

No RH premise, Xi-zero hypothesis, computation, or asymptotic interchange is used.
-/

open Complex
open scoped BigOperators

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Exact total-mass law: complete dressed marked halfgap debt is wall mass times the single
centered rank-one square. -/
theorem tsum_suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion_eq
    {h a : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) (ha : 0 < a) (t m d r s : ℝ) :
    (∑' pe : Nat.Primes × ℕ,
      suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion
        h a t m d r s pe) =
      (∑' pe : Nat.Primes × ℕ,
        Complex.normSq
          (suzukiCriticalApertureBoundaryAtom h a t pe.1 pe.2)) *
        (r - m * s) ^ 2 := by
  have hs :=
    summable_normSq_suzukiCriticalApertureBoundaryAtom_allPrime hh ha t
  rw [show (∑' pe : Nat.Primes × ℕ,
      suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion
        h a t m d r s pe) =
      ∑' pe : Nat.Primes × ℕ,
        Complex.normSq
          (suzukiCriticalApertureBoundaryAtom h a t pe.1 pe.2) *
          (r - m * s) ^ 2 by
      apply tsum_congr
      intro pe
      exact suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion_eq
        h a t m d r s pe]
  exact hs.tsum_mul_right ((r - m * s) ^ 2)

/-- Uniform cofinal ceiling.  Right side is independent of observer aperture `a`, spectral
height `t`, and halfgap coordinate `d`. -/
theorem tsum_suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion_le
    {h a : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) (ha : 0 < a) (t m d r s : ℝ) :
    (∑' pe : Nat.Primes × ℕ,
      suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion
        h a t m d r s pe) ≤
      (2 * ((h * Real.sqrt h)⁻¹) ^ 2 *
        (∑' p : Nat.Primes,
          Real.log (p : ℝ) * ((p : ℝ) ^ 2)⁻¹)) *
        (r - m * s) ^ 2 := by
  rw [tsum_suzukiCriticalApertureDressedMarkedRootedCompletion_eq
    hh ha t m d r s]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
    (tsum_normSq_suzukiCriticalApertureBoundaryAtom_allPrime_le hh ha t)
    (sq_nonneg _)

end


end RHTower

# The corpus's van der Corput could not be pointed at any Liouville phase; now it can

- **ID:** `van-der-corput-local-hypotheses`
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** INFRASTRUCTURE (formalized)
- **Scientific status:** `[LEAN-PROVED, AXIOM-CLEAN]` `[NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
  `[NOT AN RH PROOF]`
- **Module:** `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/VanDerCorputLocal.lean`,
  `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/LogChirpNonstationary.lean`

## 1. The defect

`RHTower/VanDerCorput.lean` proves the weighted first- and second-derivative tests, but states them
with **global** smoothness:

```text
firstDerivTest  : ContDiff ℝ 2 φ, ContDiff ℝ 1 A  on all of ℝ
secondDerivTest : ContDiff ℝ 2 φ, ContDiff ℝ 1 A  on all of ℝ
```

Almost no phase of interest to this project is globally `C²`:

- the exterior radial Liouville phase `ξ_σ` is singular at the turning point `z = 1`;
- the Riemann–von Mangoldt chirp `t log t` is not `C²` at `t = 0`;
- every Liouville–Green phase is smooth only on the classically allowed region.

So the tests could not be applied to any of them without first constructing a global extension —
which is real work, and which nobody did. **The obstruction was formal, not mathematical**, and it
had silently blocked the whole van der Corput lane.

## 2. What is now proved

Same statements, same constants, all hypotheses on `[a,b]` only, derivatives supplied as data:

```text
norm_le_budget_of_hasDerivAt : ‖A t‖ ≤ ‖A a‖ + ∫_a^b ‖A'‖              (local amplitude budget)
firstDerivTestOn  : |φ'| ≥ lam > 0, φ'' ≥ 0 on [a,b]
                    ==> ‖∫_a^b A e^{iφ}‖ ≤ 4 (‖A b‖+‖A a‖+∫‖A'‖)/lam
secondDerivTestOn : φ'' ≥ mu > 0 on [a,b]
                    ==> ‖∫_a^b A e^{iφ}‖ ≤ 32 (‖A b‖+‖A a‖+∫‖A'‖)/sqrt(mu)
```

Both axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## 3. First application: the log-chirp

`LogChirpNonstationary.lean`, for `φ(t) = c·t log t`, so `φ'(t) = c(log t + 1)`, `φ''(t) = c/t`:

```text
norm_integral_logChirp_le              with amplitude, second-derivative form
norm_integral_logChirp_const_le        ‖∫_T^R exp(i c t log t)‖ ≤ 64 sqrt(R)/sqrt(c)   (0 < T ≤ R)
norm_integral_logChirp_const_le_of_one_le
                                       ‖∫_T^R exp(i c t log t)‖ ≤ 8/(c (log T + 1))    (1 ≤ T ≤ R)
```

The two bounds are incomparable, and each is the better one in its own regime. The first-derivative
form does not grow with the length of the interval and is the one to use whenever `T ≥ 1`; the
second-derivative form is the only one available on an interval containing the stationary point
`t = e^{-1}` (the unique zero of `φ'`), where the first-derivative test has no lower bound to use.
Neither is claimed to be sharp.

**This is not an improvement to the Selberg lane and I am not claiming it is.** For `T` large the
*first*-derivative test is far stronger, since `φ' = c(log t + 1)` grows while `φ'' = c/t` decays:
it gives `O(1/(c log T))` on `[T,2T]`, i.e. the corpus's already-recorded
`Ψ_T(k) = O_F(1/(k d_F T))` (working log §178.1, Theorem 104), and Theorem 104 proves that rate is
the method's total unconditional content. Nothing here moves that ceiling.

What the second-derivative form does give that the first cannot: a bound that is **uniform across the
stationary point** `t = e^{-1}`, where `φ' = 0` and the first-derivative test is unavailable. Any
argument whose interval straddles `e^{-1}` needs this form.

## 4. Second application

`OscillatoryMassRetention.lean` and `RadialPSWFMassRetention.lean` — see
`oscillatory-envelope-to-relative-mass.md`. Those are the reason this file exists: the mass-retention
estimate is an application of `firstDerivTestOn` to the doubled radial phase, and it could not have
been stated with the global test.

## 5. Honest grade

Van der Corput's tests are 1920s mathematics and the local restatement changes no constant. This is
infrastructure. Its only claim on attention is that it removes a *silent* blocker: a tool the corpus
believed it had, but could not actually use on its own objects. That kind of defect is invisible
until someone tries to apply the tool, which is an argument for applying tools rather than cataloguing
them.

# Radial PSWF exterior-phase concavity/secant universality law

- **ID:** `radial-pswf-exterior-phase-concavity-secant-universality-law`
- **Law:** LAW498

## Theorem

For the radial PSWF exterior Liouville speed and normalized phase

```text
S_sigma(z) = sqrt((z^2 - sigma^2) / (z^2 - 1)),
Phi_sigma(z) = integral from 2 to z of S_sigma(u) du,
```

assume `0 <= sigma <= 1`.  On the complete exterior ray `(1, infinity)`:

1. `Phi_sigma` is concave;
2. every secant is trapped between its endpoint speeds and above the free speed:

   ```text
   1 <= S_sigma(y)
     <= (Phi_sigma(y) - Phi_sigma(x)) / (y - x)
     <= S_sigma(x)                    for 1 < x < y.
   ```

If `sigma^2 < 1`, the phase is strictly concave and both endpoint secant inequalities are strict.
Thus every finite exterior phase increment carries one sharp global law: nonstationary free-speed
floor, decreasing local speed, and strict interior averaging away from the boundary parameter.

## Theorem-generated derivation

This law was not predicted and then searched.  Whole-corpus same-folder leaf pairing exposed:

- `RadialPSWFExteriorPhase.hasDerivAt_radialPSWFExteriorPhase`;
- `RadialPSWFExteriorPhase.one_le_radialPSWFExteriorSpeed`;
- `RadialPSWFSpeedMonotone.antitoneOn_radialPSWFExteriorSpeed`;
- `RadialPSWFSpeedMonotone.hasDerivAt_radialPSWFExteriorSpeed`;
- `RadialPSWFSpeedMonotone.radialPSWFExteriorSpeed_deriv_nonpos`.

The phase derivative equals `S_sigma` at every exterior point.  Since `S_sigma` is antitone,
the derivative criterion for concavity makes `Phi_sigma` concave on `(1, infinity)`.  Concave
endpoint derivative inequalities give

```text
S_sigma(y) <= slope(Phi_sigma, x, y) <= S_sigma(x).
```

The already-proved speed floor supplies the leading `1`.  When `sigma^2 < 1`, the exact speed
derivative has positive denominator and strictly negative numerator at every exterior point.
Hence `S_sigma` is strictly antitone, the phase is strictly concave, and the endpoint inequalities
are strict.

No numerical computation is used.

## Strict corpus delta

`RadialPSWFExteriorPhase` proves only pointwise phase derivatives and a pointwise derivative floor.
`RadialPSWFSpeedMonotone` proves only speed monotonicity, its exact derivative, and separate
Liouville--Green energy signs.  Neither module promotes these local facts to concavity of the
integrated phase or controls every finite phase increment simultaneously by both endpoint speeds.
The strict secant envelope is therefore a new global finite-interval law.

Performed only after the dependency-closed Lean proof passed.

- [DLMF Chapter 30](https://dlmf.nist.gov/30.2) records spheroidal differential equations and

Targeted searches for radial/prolate spheroidal Liouville phase concavity, decreasing exterior

`[NOVELTY PLAUSIBLE — SEARCH NOT EXHAUSTIVE]`.  Generic “antitone derivative implies concavity” is

module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Nilpotent

/-!
# Newton-Raphson method

Given a single-variable polynomial `P` with derivative `P'`, Newton's method concerns iteration of
the rational map: `x ↦ x - P(x) / P'(x)`.

Over a field, it can serve as a root-finding algorithm. It is also useful in proving results such
as Hensel's lemma and the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition.

## Main definitions / results:

* `Polynomial.newtonMap`: the map `x ↦ x - P(x) / P'(x)`, where `P'` is the derivative of the
  polynomial `P`.
* `Polynomial.isFixedPt_newtonMap_of_isUnit_iff`: `x` is a fixed point for Newton iteration iff
  it is a root of `P` (provided `P'(x)` is a unit).
* `Polynomial.existsUnique_nilpotent_sub_and_aeval_eq_zero`: if `x` is almost a root of `P` in the
  sense that `P(x)` is nilpotent (and `P'(x)` is a unit) then we may write `x` as a sum
  `x = n + r` where `n` is nilpotent and `r` is a root of `P`. This can be used to prove the
  Jordan-Chevalley decomposition of linear endomorphisms.

-/

@[expose] public section

open Set Function

noncomputable section

namespace Polynomial

variable {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (P : R[X]) {x : S}

/-- Given a single-variable polynomial `P` with derivative `P'`, this is the map:
`x ↦ x - P(x) / P'(x)`. When `P'(x)` is not a unit we use a junk-value pattern and send `x ↦ x`. -/
def newtonMap (x : S) : S :=
  x - (Ring.inverse <| aeval x (derivative P)) * aeval x P

theorem newtonMap_apply :
    P.newtonMap x = x - (Ring.inverse <| aeval x (derivative P)) * (aeval x P) :=
  rfl

variable {P}

theorem newtonMap_apply_of_isUnit (h : IsUnit <| aeval x (derivative P)) :
    P.newtonMap x = x - h.unit⁻¹ * aeval x P := by
  simp [newtonMap_apply, Ring.inverse, h]

theorem newtonMap_apply_of_not_isUnit (h : ¬ (IsUnit <| aeval x (derivative P))) :
    P.newtonMap x = x := by
  simp [newtonMap_apply, Ring.inverse, h]

theorem isNilpotent_iterate_newtonMap_sub_of_isNilpotent (h : IsNilpotent <| aeval x P) (n : ℕ) :
    IsNilpotent <| P.newtonMap^[n] x - x := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [iterate_succ', comp_apply, newtonMap_apply, sub_right_comm]
    refine (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_sub ih <| (Commute.all _ _).isNilpotent_mul_left ?_
    simpa using Commute.isNilpotent_add (Commute.all _ _)
      (isNilpotent_aeval_sub_of_isNilpotent_sub P ih) h

theorem isFixedPt_newtonMap_of_aeval_eq_zero (h : aeval x P = 0) :
    IsFixedPt P.newtonMap x := by
  rw [IsFixedPt, newtonMap_apply, h, mul_zero, sub_zero]

theorem isFixedPt_newtonMap_of_isUnit_iff (h : IsUnit <| aeval x (derivative P)) :
    IsFixedPt P.newtonMap x ↔ aeval x P = 0 := by
  rw [IsFixedPt, newtonMap_apply, sub_eq_self, Ring.inverse_mul_eq_iff_eq_mul _ _ _ h, mul_zero]

/-- This is really an auxiliary result, en route to
`Polynomial.existsUnique_nilpotent_sub_and_aeval_eq_zero`. -/
theorem aeval_pow_two_pow_dvd_aeval_iterate_newtonMap
    (h : IsNilpotent (aeval x P)) (h' : IsUnit (aeval x <| derivative P)) (n : ℕ) :
    (aeval x P) ^ (2 ^ n) ∣ aeval (P.newtonMap^[n] x) P := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    have ⟨d, hd⟩ := binomExpansion (P.map (algebraMap R S)) (P.newtonMap^[n] x)
      (-Ring.inverse (aeval (P.newtonMap^[n] x) <| derivative P) * aeval (P.newtonMap^[n] x) P)
    rw [eval_map_algebraMap, eval_map_algebraMap] at hd
    rw [iterate_succ', comp_apply, newtonMap_apply, sub_eq_add_neg, neg_mul_eq_neg_mul, hd]
    refine dvd_add ?_ (dvd_mul_of_dvd_right ?_ _)
    · convert! dvd_zero _
      have : IsUnit (aeval (P.newtonMap^[n] x) <| derivative P) :=
        isUnit_aeval_of_isUnit_aeval_of_isNilpotent_sub h' <|
        isNilpotent_iterate_newtonMap_sub_of_isNilpotent h n
      rw [derivative_map, eval_map_algebraMap, ← mul_assoc, mul_neg, Ring.mul_inverse_cancel _ this,
        neg_mul, one_mul, add_neg_cancel]
    · rw [neg_mul, even_two.neg_pow, mul_pow, pow_succ, pow_mul]
      exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (pow_dvd_pow_of_dvd ih 2) _

/-- If `x` is almost a root of `P` in the sense that `P(x)` is nilpotent (and `P'(x)` is a
unit) then we may write `x` as a sum `x = n + r` where `n` is nilpotent and `r` is a root of `P`.
Moreover, `n` and `r` are unique.

This can be used to prove the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition of linear endomorphisms. -/
theorem existsUnique_nilpotent_sub_and_aeval_eq_zero
    (h : IsNilpotent (aeval x P)) (h' : IsUnit (aeval x <| derivative P)) :
    ∃! r, IsNilpotent (x - r) ∧ aeval r P = 0 := by
  simp_rw [(neg_sub _ x).symm, isNilpotent_neg_iff]
  refine existsUnique_of_exists_of_unique ?_ fun r₁ r₂ ⟨hr₁, hr₁'⟩ ⟨hr₂, hr₂'⟩ ↦ ?_
  · -- Existence
    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := id h
    refine ⟨P.newtonMap^[n] x, isNilpotent_iterate_newtonMap_sub_of_isNilpotent h n, ?_⟩

/-
The van der Corput derivative tests, indexed by order, and the optimality of the third.

The classical `k`-th derivative test corresponds to the exponent pair

    **(κ_k, λ_k) = ( 1/(2^k - 2) ,  1 - (k-1)/(2^k - 2) )** ,   `k ≥ 3` ,

which is exactly the tower produced by iterating the `A`-process from `B(0,1)`, with `k = j + 2`.  So
the closed form obtained earlier from the `A`-recursion is the classical one, an independent
confirmation.

Its subconvexity exponent is

    **μ_k = 1/4 - (k-2) / (2(2^k - 2))** ,

which equals `1/6` at `k = 3` — Weyl's exponent — and **increases** with `k` toward the convexity
bound `1/4`:

    k = 3 : **1/6 = 0.166667** ,   k = 4 : **5/28 = 0.178571** ,
    k = 5 : **1/5 = 0.2** ,        k = 6 : **27/124 = 0.217742** .

So **the third derivative test is the best of the family at the critical line**, and every
higher-order test is strictly worse there — while, by the earlier scale analysis, the higher tests are
the ones that clear the small block scales.  That is the classical reason Weyl's `1/6` was the
baseline for sixty-five years: no order of van der Corput's method improves it.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ClassDecompositionNotAReduction

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The tests, indexed by order -/

/-- Denominator `2^k - 2` of the `k`-th derivative test. -/
def testDen (k : ℕ) : ℚ := 2 ^ k - 2

/-- First coordinate of the `k`-th test's exponent pair. -/
def testKappa (k : ℕ) : ℚ := 1 / testDen k

/-- Second coordinate. -/
def testLambda (k : ℕ) : ℚ := 1 - (k - 1) / testDen k

/-- Its subconvexity exponent. -/
def testMu (k : ℕ) : ℚ := 1 / 4 - (k - 2) / (2 * testDen k)

/-- **The `k`-th test is the `(k-2)`-nd member of the `A`-tower.** -/
theorem test_is_tower (j : ℕ) :
    testDen (j + 2) = towerDen j ∧ testKappa (j + 2) = towerKappa j := by
  constructor
  · unfold testDen towerDen; norm_num
  · unfold testKappa towerKappa
    congr 1

/-- And the second coordinates agree. -/
theorem test_lambda_is_tower (j : ℕ) : testLambda (j + 2) = towerLambda j := by
  unfold testLambda towerLambda
  rw [(test_is_tower j).1]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- **The exponents agree too.** -/
theorem test_mu_is_tower (j : ℕ) : testMu (j + 2) = towerMu j := by
  unfold testMu towerMu
  rw [(test_is_tower j).1]
  push_cast
  ring

/-! ### Values -/

theorem testDen_values :
    testDen 3 = 6 ∧ testDen 4 = 14 ∧ testDen 5 = 30 ∧ testDen 6 = 62 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> (unfold testDen; norm_num)

/-- **The third test is Weyl's.** -/
@[simp] theorem testMu_three : testMu 3 = 1 / 6 := by
  unfold testMu testDen; norm_num

@[simp] theorem testMu_four : testMu 4 = 5 / 28 := by
  unfold testMu testDen; norm_num

@[simp] theorem testMu_five : testMu 5 = 1 / 5 := by
  unfold testMu testDen; norm_num

@[simp] theorem testMu_six : testMu 6 = 27 / 124 := by
  unfold testMu testDen; norm_num

/-- **The exponents increase with the order.** -/
theorem testMu_increasing :
    testMu 3 < testMu 4 ∧ testMu 4 < testMu 5 ∧ testMu 5 < testMu 6 := by
  rw [testMu_three, testMu_four, testMu_five, testMu_six]
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- **And stay below the convexity bound.** -/
theorem testMu_below_convexity : testMu 6 < 1 / 4 := by
  rw [testMu_six]; norm_num

/-! ### Optimality of the third test -/

/-- **Weyl's exponent is the best in the family.** -/
theorem third_test_optimal :
    testMu 3 < testMu 4 ∧ testMu 3 < testMu 5 ∧ testMu 3 < testMu 6 := by
  rw [testMu_three, testMu_four, testMu_five, testMu_six]
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- **And it is Weyl's `1/6`, the pre-1986 baseline.** -/
theorem third_test_is_weyl : testMu 3 = weylKappa := by
  rw [testMu_three]; unfold weylKappa; rfl

/-- **The record lies strictly below the whole family**, which is why every improvement since Weyl has
come from outside van der Corput's method. -/
theorem record_below_family :
    bourgainTheta < testMu 3 ∧ bourgainTheta < testMu 4 ∧ bourgainTheta < testMu 5 := by
  rw [testMu_three, testMu_four, testMu_five]
  unfold bourgainTheta
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- **Summary.**  The derivative tests form the `A`-tower; their critical-line exponents increase from
Weyl's `1/6` toward `1/4`; the third is optimal; and the record `13/84` lies below all of them. -/
theorem derivative_test_summary :
    testMu 3 = 1 / 6 ∧ testMu 3 < testMu 4 ∧ testMu 6 < 1 / 4 ∧ bourgainTheta < testMu 3 :=
  ⟨testMu_three, testMu_increasing.1, testMu_below_convexity, record_below_family.1⟩

end HTGeometry

/-!
# A bounded Weyl character retains its unbounded generator in its tangent value

For a real charge `q`, the scalar one-parameter unitary character

```text
chi_q(t) = exp(-i q t)
```

has unit modulus on the real parameter axis, while its derivative at the identity is
`-i q`.  Consequently `i chi_q'(0) = q`.  A uniformly bounded family of phase values can
therefore retain an unbounded charge in its tangent without asking any one bounded observable to
equal that charge.

This is the scalar value core of the Weyl/Stone description of a one-parameter quantum symmetry.
It is useful in the hypertranscendental constraint corpus whenever a fixed bounded response is too
small but a differentiable phase character is available.  No operator generator, domain claim, or
flow equation is asserted here.

Primary provenance: H. Weyl, *Quantenmechanik und Gruppentheorie*, Z. Phys. 46 (1927), 1--46,
DOI 10.1007/BF02055756; M. H. Stone, *Linear Transformations in Hilbert Space. III. Operational
Methods and Group Theory*, PNAS 16 (1930), 172--175, DOI 10.1073/pnas.16.2.172; E. P. Wigner,
*Lower Limit for the Energy Derivative of the Scattering Phase Shift*, Phys. Rev. 98 (1955),
145--147, DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.98.145; F. T. Smith, *Lifetime Matrix in Collision Theory*,
Phys. Rev. 118 (1960), 349--356, DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.118.349.
-/

namespace HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Scalar Weyl character with real generator/charge `q`.  The complex parameter keeps the
derivative statement inside ordinary complex analysis; its restriction to the real axis is
unitary. -/
def scalarWeylCharacter (q : ℝ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.exp (-Complex.I * (q : ℂ) * z)

@[simp]
theorem scalarWeylCharacter_zero (q : ℝ) :
    scalarWeylCharacter q 0 = 1 := by
  simp [scalarWeylCharacter]

/-- Characters add their generators by multiplication. -/
theorem scalarWeylCharacter_add_charge (q r : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    scalarWeylCharacter (q + r) z =
      scalarWeylCharacter q z * scalarWeylCharacter r z := by
  simp only [scalarWeylCharacter]
  rw [← Complex.exp_add]
  push_cast
  congr 1
  ring

/-- The Weyl character is a one-parameter representation of the additive parameter group. -/
theorem scalarWeylCharacter_add_parameter (q : ℝ) (z w : ℂ) :
    scalarWeylCharacter q (z + w) =
      scalarWeylCharacter q z * scalarWeylCharacter q w := by
  simp only [scalarWeylCharacter]
  rw [← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- Every real-parameter phase value has exactly unit norm, independently of the size of its
generator. -/
theorem norm_scalarWeylCharacter_ofReal (q t : ℝ) :
    ‖scalarWeylCharacter q (t : ℂ)‖ = 1 := by
  rw [scalarWeylCharacter, Complex.norm_exp]
  have hre : (-Complex.I * (q : ℂ) * (t : ℂ)).re = 0 := by
    simp
  rw [hre, Real.exp_zero]

/-- Differential form of the scalar Weyl law. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_scalarWeylCharacter (q : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    HasDerivAt (scalarWeylCharacter q)
      (-Complex.I * (q : ℂ) * scalarWeylCharacter q z) z := by
  have hlinear :
      HasDerivAt (fun w : ℂ => -Complex.I * (q : ℂ) * w)
        (-Complex.I * (q : ℂ)) z := by
    simpa using (hasDerivAt_id z).const_mul (-Complex.I * (q : ℂ))
  rw [scalarWeylCharacter]
  exact hlinear.cexp.congr_deriv (by ring)

/-- Pointwise derivative of the scalar Weyl character. -/
theorem deriv_scalarWeylCharacter (q : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    deriv (scalarWeylCharacter q) z =
      -Complex.I * (q : ℂ) * scalarWeylCharacter q z :=
  (hasDerivAt_scalarWeylCharacter q z).deriv

/-- The tangent of the bounded character at the identity is its skew generator. -/
@[simp]
theorem deriv_scalarWeylCharacter_zero (q : ℝ) :
    deriv (scalarWeylCharacter q) 0 = -Complex.I * (q : ℂ) := by
  rw [deriv_scalarWeylCharacter]
  simp

/-- **Stone generator value.**  Multiplication by `i` recovers the full real charge from the
identity tangent of the unit-modulus character. -/
theorem I_mul_deriv_scalarWeylCharacter_zero (q : ℝ) :
    Complex.I * deriv (scalarWeylCharacter q) 0 = (q : ℂ) := by
  rw [deriv_scalarWeylCharacter_zero]
  calc
    Complex.I * (-Complex.I * (q : ℂ)) =
        -(Complex.I * Complex.I) * (q : ℂ) := by ring
    _ = (q : ℂ) := by rw [Complex.I_mul_I]; ring

/-- A fixed bound on all real phase values imposes no bound on the recovered tangent charge.  This
is the precise value-level escape from arguments that try to represent a growing source by one
fixed bounded detector. -/
theorem scalarWeylCharacter_bounded_and_generator_exact (q : ℝ) :
    (∀ t : ℝ, ‖scalarWeylCharacter q (t : ℂ)‖ = 1) ∧
      Complex.I * deriv (scalarWeylCharacter q) 0 = (q : ℂ) := by
  exact ⟨norm_scalarWeylCharacter_ofReal q,
    I_mul_deriv_scalarWeylCharacter_zero q⟩

/-- **Scalar Wigner--Smith value.**  The relative phase derivative recovers the same real charge
at every real parameter, not only at the identity.  The conjugate phase removes the arbitrary
point on the unitary orbit. -/

/-!
# The characteristic clock equation is ill posed for non-analytic transverse data

The clock construction solves

`∂ξ∂η u = (∑ᵢ ∂ᵢ²u + V u)/4`

by the Ovsyannikov scheme, which asks the transverse dependence to be *analytic*. That hypothesis is
not an artifact of the method. In the transverse directions the equation is elliptic — a second
derivative appears there while the null directions carry one derivative each — so the characteristic
problem inherits Hadamard's phenomenon: arbitrarily small characteristic data can produce arbitrarily
large solutions.

This file proves that, in the sharpest elementary form. The exact solutions

`u_{k,n}(ξ, η, z) = e^{-n/2} n^{-k} · exp(n ξ/2 + n η/2 + n z)`

solve the equation with `V = 0`, are bounded by `n^{-k}` on the two characteristic faces of the unit
box together with all their transverse derivatives of order below `k`, and take the value
`e^{n/2} n^{-k}` at the far corner. So no estimate bounding the solution at an interior point by any
function of finitely many transverse derivatives of the characteristic data can hold: the smooth
category is out of reach for this route, and reaching it requires the Cauchy problem on a spacelike
hypersurface rather than the characteristic one.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Filter

/-! ## Derivatives of an affine exponential -/

theorem hasDerivAt_expAffine (a b x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun w : ℝ => Real.exp (a * w + b)) (a * Real.exp (a * x + b)) x := by
  have hinner : HasDerivAt (fun w : ℝ => a * w + b) a x := by
    simpa using ((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul a).add_const b
  have h := (Real.hasDerivAt_exp (a * x + b)).comp x hinner
  rw [show a * Real.exp (a * x + b) = Real.exp (a * x + b) * a from by ring]
  exact h

theorem deriv_expAffine (a b : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun w : ℝ => Real.exp (a * w + b)) = fun x => a * Real.exp (a * x + b) := by
  funext x
  exact (hasDerivAt_expAffine a b x).deriv

theorem iteratedDeriv_scaledExpAffine (j : ℕ) (c a b : ℝ) :
    iteratedDeriv j (fun w : ℝ => c * Real.exp (a * w + b))
      = fun x => c * a ^ j * Real.exp (a * x + b) := by
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    funext x
    simp [iteratedDeriv_zero]
  | succ j ih =>
    funext x
    have hd : HasDerivAt (fun w : ℝ => c * a ^ j * Real.exp (a * w + b))
        (c * a ^ (j + 1) * Real.exp (a * x + b)) x := by
      have h := (hasDerivAt_expAffine a b x).const_mul (c * a ^ j)
      rw [show c * a ^ (j + 1) * Real.exp (a * x + b)
        = c * a ^ j * (a * Real.exp (a * x + b)) from by ring]
      exact h
    rw [iteratedDeriv_succ, ih]
    exact hd.deriv

/-! ## The Hadamard family for the characteristic equation -/

/-- The normalising factor: the family is scaled so that its characteristic data is at most
`n^{-k}`. -/
noncomputable def hadamardScale (k n : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.exp (-(n : ℝ) / 2) / (n : ℝ) ^ k

/-- An exact solution of `∂ξ∂η u = ∂_z²u/4` with characteristic data of size `n^{-k}`. -/
noncomputable def hadamardWave (k n : ℕ) (ξ η z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  hadamardScale k n * Real.exp ((n : ℝ) / 2 * ξ + (n : ℝ) / 2 * η + (n : ℝ) * z)

theorem hadamardScale_nonneg (k n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ hadamardScale k n := by
  rw [hadamardScale]
  positivity

theorem hadamardWave_pos (k n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (ξ η z : ℝ) : 0 < hadamardWave k n ξ η z := by
  have hs : 0 < hadamardScale k n := by
    rw [hadamardScale]
    have : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) ^ k := by
      have : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
      positivity
    positivity
  rw [hadamardWave]
  positivity

/-- The derivative along the first null coordinate. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_hadamardWave_fst (k n : ℕ) (ξ η z : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => hadamardWave k n x η z)
      ((n : ℝ) / 2 * hadamardWave k n ξ η z) ξ := by
  have hEq : (fun x : ℝ => hadamardWave k n x η z)
      = fun x : ℝ => hadamardScale k n
        * Real.exp ((n : ℝ) / 2 * x + ((n : ℝ) / 2 * η + (n : ℝ) * z)) := by
    funext x
    rw [hadamardWave]
    ring_nf
  rw [hEq]
  have hbase := (hasDerivAt_expAffine ((n : ℝ) / 2) ((n : ℝ) / 2 * η + (n : ℝ) * z) ξ).const_mul
    (hadamardScale k n)
  refine hbase.congr_deriv ?_
  rw [hadamardWave]
  ring_nf

/-- The derivative along the second null coordinate. -/
theorem hasDerivAt_hadamardWave_snd (k n : ℕ) (ξ η z : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => hadamardWave k n ξ y z)
      ((n : ℝ) / 2 * hadamardWave k n ξ η z) η := by
  have hEq : (fun y : ℝ => hadamardWave k n ξ y z)
      = fun y : ℝ => hadamardScale k n
        * Real.exp ((n : ℝ) / 2 * y + ((n : ℝ) / 2 * ξ + (n : ℝ) * z)) := by
    funext y
    rw [hadamardWave]
    ring_nf
  rw [hEq]
  have hbase := (hasDerivAt_expAffine ((n : ℝ) / 2) ((n : ℝ) / 2 * ξ + (n : ℝ) * z) η).const_mul
    (hadamardScale k n)
  refine hbase.congr_deriv ?_
  rw [hadamardWave]
  ring_nf

/-- **The second-derivative log-derivative identity for Γ.**  At any point where `Γ` is twice
differentiable and nonzero, `Γ''·Γ − (Γ')² = Γ²·(Γ'/Γ)'` — the numerator of the quotient rule for the
log-derivative `ψ = Γ'/Γ`.  This is the algebraic core connecting Γ's second-order jet to the digamma:
the combination `Γ·Γ'' − (Γ')²`, which is exactly the leading obstruction in the mixed
`(Γ')²`/`Γ·Γ''` tie, equals `Γ²·ψ'`. -/
theorem gamma_secondDeriv_logDeriv_identity (s : ℂ) (hs : Complex.Gamma s ≠ 0)
    (h1 : DifferentiableAt ℂ Complex.Gamma s) (h2 : DifferentiableAt ℂ (deriv Complex.Gamma) s) :
    iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s - (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
      = (Complex.Gamma s)^2 * deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s := by
  have hdd : deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s
      = (deriv (deriv Complex.Gamma) s * Complex.Gamma s
        - deriv Complex.Gamma s * deriv Complex.Gamma s) / (Complex.Gamma s)^2 :=
    deriv_div h2 h1 hs
  rw [hdd, show iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s = deriv (deriv Complex.Gamma) s from by
    rw [iteratedDeriv_succ, iteratedDeriv_one]]
  field_simp

/-- **The mixed three-variable relation reduces to a first-order relation in the digamma jet.**  If
`α(s)·(Γ')² + β(s)·(Γ''·Γ) = 0` at a point where `Γ` is twice differentiable and nonzero, then
`(α+β)(s)·ψ² + β(s)·ψ' = 0` there, for the log-derivative `ψ = Γ'/Γ` (digamma).  Substituting the
identity `Γ·Γ'' = (Γ')² + Γ²·ψ'` and dividing by `Γ²` collapses the three jet variables `(Γ,Γ',Γ'')`
— where the `(Γ')²`/`Γ·Γ''` monomial tie obstructs the residue method — to two jet variables `(ψ,ψ')`.
This is the bridge that turns the sole remaining tie-obstructed case of Hölder's theorem for `Γ` into a
differential-non-existence question for the digamma. -/
theorem gamma_mixed_reduces_to_digamma (α β : Polynomial ℂ) (s : ℂ) (hs : Complex.Gamma s ≠ 0)
    (h1 : DifferentiableAt ℂ Complex.Gamma s) (h2 : DifferentiableAt ℂ (deriv Complex.Gamma) s)
    (hrel : α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
      + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s) = 0) :
    (α.eval s + β.eval s) * (deriv Complex.Gamma s / Complex.Gamma s)^2
      + β.eval s * deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s = 0 := by
  have hid := gamma_secondDeriv_logDeriv_identity s hs h1 h2
  have hΓ2 : (Complex.Gamma s)^2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hs
  field_simp
  have key : α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
      + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s) = 0 := hrel
  rw [show iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s
    = (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2 + (Complex.Gamma s)^2 * deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s
    from by linear_combination hid] at key
  linear_combination key

/-- **The leading constraint on the mixed three-variable relation.**  If
`α(s)·(Γ')² + β(s)·(Γ''·Γ) = 0` off the poles, then `α + 2β = 0` as polynomials.  The two monomials
`(Γ')²` and `Γ·Γ''` both have weighted degree `4` and total degree `2` — the genuine tie — so at each
pole `−k` their leading Laurent coefficients add on the *same* power `r_k²`: multiplying by `(s+k)⁴` and
letting `s → −k` gives `(α(−k) + 2β(−k))·r_k² = 0`, hence `α(−k) + 2β(−k) = 0` for every `k` (residues
`(s+k)²Γ' → −r_k`, `(s+k)Γ·(s+k)³Γ'' → 2r_k²`).  Since `α + 2β` vanishes at the infinitely many points
`−k`, it is the zero polynomial.  Combined with the identity `Γ·Γ'' − 2(Γ')² = Γ²·(ψ' − ψ²)`
(`gamma_secondDeriv_logDeriv_identity`), this reduces the mixed case to `β·Γ²·(ψ' − ψ²) = 0`: the whole
tie collapses to `β = 0` once `ψ' − ψ²` (digamma) is shown not identically zero — the sole surviving
crux of Hölder's theorem for `Γ` in three jet variables. -/
theorem gamma_mixed_leading (α β : Polynomial ℂ)
    (hrel : ∀ s : ℂ, (∀ m : ℕ, s ≠ -(m:ℂ)) →
      α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
        + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s) = 0) :
    α + 2 * β = 0 := by
  have hroot : ∀ k : ℕ, (α + 2 * β).eval (-(k:ℂ)) = 0 := by
    intro k
    have hlim0 : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => (s + (k:ℂ))^4 *
        (α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
          + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s)))
        (𝓝[≠] (-(k:ℂ))) (𝓝 0) := by
      have hev : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[≠] (-(k:ℂ)), (s + (k:ℂ))^4 *
          (α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
            + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s)) = 0 := by
        filter_upwards [eventually_nhdsWithin_of_eventually_nhds
          (Metric.ball_mem_nhds (-(k:ℂ)) (show (0:ℝ) < 1/2 by norm_num)), self_mem_nhdsWithin]
          with s hsb hsne
        simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hsne
        rw [hrel s (ball_avoids hsb hsne), mul_zero]
      exact tendsto_const_nhds.congr' (hev.mono (fun _ h => h.symm))
    have hcα : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => α.eval s) (𝓝[≠] (-(k:ℂ))) (𝓝 (α.eval (-(k:ℂ)))) :=
      α.continuous.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt

/-!
# Exceptional Selberg parameters in the compact principal-series model

Every scalar `0 < λ < 1/4` is realized by the normalized finite compact-picture complementary
series with parameter `s = 2 sqrt(1/4-λ)`.  Its shifted Casimir is `λ`, its positive invariant
form exists, and its Harish-Chandra module is irreducible.  This is the concrete local endpoint of
the Maass-to-representation part of the symmetric-power strategy.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Exceptional parameter belongs to the exact compact-picture unitarity locus. -/
theorem SelbergExceptionalEigenvalue.compactLocalParameter_unitarizable
    (eigenvalue : SelbergExceptionalEigenvalue) :
    2 * eigenvalue.complementaryExponent ∈
      UnitarizableCompactSphericalPrincipalParameter := by
  rw [unitarizableCompactSphericalPrincipalParameter_eq_Ioo]
  have hν := eigenvalue.complementaryExponent_mem_Ioo
  rcases hν with ⟨hνpos, hνhalf⟩
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- Shifted compact-picture Casimir has the exceptional eigenvalue as its scalar. -/
theorem SelbergExceptionalEigenvalue.compactSphericalPrincipalLaplacian_eq
    (eigenvalue : SelbergExceptionalEigenvalue) :
    compactSphericalPrincipalLaplacian
        (2 * eigenvalue.complementaryExponent) =
      (eigenvalue.1 : ℂ) • LinearMap.id := by
  rw [compactSphericalPrincipalLaplacian_eq_smul_id]
  congr 1
  norm_cast
  rw [← eigenvalue.eigenvalueOfComplementaryExponent_eq]
  simp [eigenvalueOfComplementaryExponent]
  ring

/-- Exceptional compact-picture Harish-Chandra module is irreducible. -/
theorem SelbergExceptionalEigenvalue.compactSphericalPrincipal_irreducible
    (eigenvalue : SelbergExceptionalEigenvalue) :
    ∀ W : Submodule ℂ
        (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule
          (2 * eigenvalue.complementaryExponent)),
      IsCompactSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule
          (2 * eigenvalue.complementaryExponent) W →
        W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤ := by
  apply compactSphericalPrincipal_irreducible_of_abs_lt_one
  have hν := eigenvalue.complementaryExponent_mem_Ioo
  rcases hν with ⟨hνpos, hνhalf⟩
  rw [abs_lt]
  constructor <;> linarith

end
end GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower
