/-!
# Complementary-series unitarity in the compact picture

The explicit complementary-series Hermitian form is transported to the finite normalized
compact-picture principal series.  Positivity and `e† = -f` invariance are proved in both
directions across the Fourier equivalence, giving the exact compact-picture unitarity locus
`(-1,1)` without assuming an exponent bound.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Pull back a complex Hermitian form along a complex-linear map in both variables. -/
def pullbackComplexHermitianForm {V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℂ V]
    [AddCommMonoid W] [Module ℂ W] (B : ComplexHermitianForm V) (e : W →ₗ[ℂ] V) :
    ComplexHermitianForm W :=
  LinearMap.mk₂'ₛₗ (starRingEnd ℂ) (RingHom.id ℂ)
    (fun v w ↦ B (e v) (e w))
    (by intro; simp)
    (by intro; simp)
    (by intro; simp)
    (by intro; simp)

@[simp]
theorem pullbackComplexHermitianForm_apply {V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℂ V]
    [AddCommMonoid W] [Module ℂ W] (B : ComplexHermitianForm V) (e : W →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (v w : W) : pullbackComplexHermitianForm B e v w = B (e v) (e w) :=
  rfl

/-- Complementary-series Hermitian form on finite compact-picture K-types. -/
def compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm (s : ℝ) :
    ComplexHermitianForm (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :=
  pullbackComplexHermitianForm (sphericalComplementaryHermitianForm s)
    (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).symm.toLinearMap

@[simp]
theorem compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm_apply (s : ℝ)
    (v w : normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :
    compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm s v w =
      sphericalComplementaryHermitianForm s
        ((sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).symm v)
        ((sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).symm w) :=
  rfl

/-- Infinitesimal invariance relation on finite compact-picture K-types. -/
def IsCompactSphericalPrincipalInvariant (s : ℝ)
    (B : ComplexHermitianForm (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s)) : Prop :=
  ∀ v w,
    B (compactSphericalPrincipalE s v) w =
      -B v (compactSphericalPrincipalF s w)

theorem compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm_positiveDefinite
    (s : ℝ) (hs : |s| < 1) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteHermitian (compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm s) := by
  have hsource := sphericalComplementaryHermitianForm_positiveDefinite s hs
  constructor
  · constructor
    intro v w
    exact hsource.1.eq
      ((sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).symm v)
      ((sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).symm w)
  · intro v hv
    apply hsource.2
    exact (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).symm.map_ne_zero_iff.mpr hv

theorem compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm_invariant
    (s : ℝ) (hs : |s| < 1) :
    IsCompactSphericalPrincipalInvariant s
      (compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm s) := by
  intro v w
  rcases (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).surjective v with ⟨x, rfl⟩
  rcases (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).surjective w with ⟨y, rfl⟩
  simpa using sphericalComplementaryHermitianForm_invariant s hs x y

/-- Compact-picture parameters admitting a positive-definite infinitesimally invariant form. -/
def UnitarizableCompactSphericalPrincipalParameter : Set ℝ :=
  {s | ∃ B : ComplexHermitianForm (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s),
    IsPositiveDefiniteHermitian B ∧ IsCompactSphericalPrincipalInvariant s B}

theorem mem_unitarizableCompactSphericalPrincipalParameter
    (s : ℝ) (hs : |s| < 1) :
    s ∈ UnitarizableCompactSphericalPrincipalParameter := by
  exact ⟨compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm s,
    compactSphericalComplementaryHermitianForm_positiveDefinite s hs,

/-!
# Irreducibility in the compact principal-series picture

The complementary-series irreducibility theorem is transferred to the normalized finite
compact-picture subspace.  Compact K-type projections are defined on the actual Fourier-function
model, and closure under those projections and the transported raising/lowering operators admits
no proper nonzero submodule for `|s| < 1`.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Projection onto one spherical weight in the finite-support model. -/
def sphericalKTypeProjection (m : ℤ) : Module.End ℂ SphericalKFiniteModel where
  toFun v := Finsupp.single m (v m)
  map_add' v w := by
    ext j
    by_cases h : m = j <;> simp [h]
  map_smul' c v := by
    ext j
    by_cases h : m = j <;> simp [h]

/-- Projection onto one even Fourier K-type in the normalized compact picture. -/
def compactSphericalKTypeProjection (s : ℝ) (m : ℤ) :
    Module.End ℂ (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :=
  (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).conj (sphericalKTypeProjection m)

@[simp]
theorem compactSphericalKTypeProjection_equiv_apply (s : ℝ) (m : ℤ)
    (v : SphericalKFiniteModel) :
    compactSphericalKTypeProjection s m (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s v) =
      sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s (Finsupp.single m (v m)) := by
  simp [compactSphericalKTypeProjection, sphericalKTypeProjection,
    LinearEquiv.conj_apply]

/-- A `(g,K)`-submodule inside the finite compact-picture principal series. -/
def IsCompactSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule (s : ℝ)
    (W : Submodule ℂ (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s)) : Prop :=
  (∀ v ∈ W, ∀ m : ℤ, compactSphericalKTypeProjection s m v ∈ W) ∧
    (∀ v ∈ W, compactSphericalPrincipalE s v ∈ W) ∧
      ∀ v ∈ W, compactSphericalPrincipalF s v ∈ W

theorem isSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule_comap_compact
    (s : ℝ) (W : Submodule ℂ (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s))
    (hW : IsCompactSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule s W) :
    IsSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule s
      (W.comap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).toLinearMap) := by
  constructor
  · intro v hv m
    change sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s (Finsupp.single m (v m)) ∈ W
    simpa using hW.1 (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s v) hv m
  constructor
  · intro v hv
    change sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s (sphericalPrincipalE (s : ℂ) v) ∈ W
    simpa using hW.2.1 (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s v) hv
  · intro v hv
    change sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s (sphericalPrincipalF (s : ℂ) v) ∈ W
    simpa using hW.2.2 (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s v) hv

/-- The normalized finite compact-picture Harish-Chandra module is irreducible throughout the
complementary interval. -/
theorem compactSphericalPrincipal_irreducible_of_abs_lt_one (s : ℝ) (hs : |s| < 1) :
    ∀ W : Submodule ℂ (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s),
      IsCompactSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule s W → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤ := by
  intro W hW
  rcases sphericalPrincipal_irreducible_of_abs_lt_one s hs
      (W.comap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).toLinearMap)
      (isSphericalHarishChandraSubmodule_comap_compact s W hW) with hbot | htop
  · left
    calc
      W = (Submodule.orderIsoMapComap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s))
          (W.comap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).toLinearMap) := by
        exact (Submodule.map_comap_eq_of_surjective
          (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).surjective W).symm
      _ = (Submodule.orderIsoMapComap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s)) ⊥ := by
        rw [hbot]
      _ = ⊥ := by simp
  · right
    calc
      W = (Submodule.orderIsoMapComap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s))
          (W.comap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).toLinearMap) := by
        exact (Submodule.map_comap_eq_of_surjective
          (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).surjective W).symm
      _ = (Submodule.orderIsoMapComap (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s)) ⊤ := by
        rw [htop]
      _ = ⊤ := by simp

end

/-!
# Principal-series action in the compact picture

The algebraically coinduced right-translation representation is conjugated through the Iwasawa
compact-picture equivalence.  The resulting action has the explicit formula
`(πσ(g)φ)(k) = χσ(b(kg)) φ(k(kg))`.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

private theorem compactPicture_conj_comp {V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [AddCommMonoid W]
    [Module ℂ V] [Module ℂ W] (e : V ≃ₗ[ℂ] W) (A B : Module.End ℂ V) :
    e.conj (A.comp B) = (e.conj A).comp (e.conj B) := by
  ext w
  rcases e.surjective w with ⟨v, rfl⟩
  simp [LinearEquiv.conj_apply]

private theorem compactPicture_conj_id {V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [AddCommMonoid W]
    [Module ℂ V] [Module ℂ W] (e : V ≃ₗ[ℂ] W) :
    e.conj LinearMap.id = LinearMap.id := by
  ext w
  rcases e.surjective w with ⟨v, rfl⟩
  simp [LinearEquiv.conj_apply]

/-- Algebraic principal-series representation transported to the compact picture. -/
def compactRealPrincipalSeries (σ : ℝ) :
    Representation ℂ SL2R (realCompactPictureSpace σ) where
  toFun g := (algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ).conj
    (algebraicRealPrincipalSeries σ g)
  map_one' := by
    rw [map_one]
    simp only [Module.End.one_eq_id]
    exact compactPicture_conj_id (algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ)
  map_mul' g h := by
    rw [map_mul]
    simp only [Module.End.mul_eq_comp]
    exact compactPicture_conj_comp (algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ) _ _

/-- Restriction to `K` intertwines coinduced right translation with compact-picture action. -/
theorem realPrincipalSeriesRestrictToK_intertwines (σ : ℝ) (g : SL2R)
    (f : Representation.coindV realUpperBorel.subtype
      (realUpperBorelExponentRepresentation σ)) :
    realPrincipalSeriesRestrictToK σ ((algebraicRealPrincipalSeries σ) g f) =
      compactRealPrincipalSeries σ g (realPrincipalSeriesRestrictToK σ f) := by
  change (algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ)
      ((algebraicRealPrincipalSeries σ) g f) =
    (algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ)
      ((algebraicRealPrincipalSeries σ) g
        ((algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ).symm
          ((algebraicRealPrincipalSeriesCompactPicture σ) f)))
  rw [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply]

/-- Explicit Iwasawa formula for the principal-series action on compact-picture functions. -/
@[simp]
theorem compactRealPrincipalSeries_apply (σ : ℝ) (g : SL2R)
    (φ : realCompactPictureSpace σ) (k : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer) :
    ((compactRealPrincipalSeries σ) g φ).1 k =
      realUpperBorelRpowCharacter σ
          (realIwasawaB ((k : SL2R) * g)) *
        φ.1 (realIwasawaK ((k : SL2R) * g)) := by
  rfl

/-- Evaluate the compact-picture action using any explicit `B K` factorization of `k g`. -/
theorem compactRealPrincipalSeries_factor_apply (σ : ℝ) (g : SL2R)
    (k : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer) (φ : realCompactPictureSpace σ)
    (b : realUpperBorel) (q : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer)
    (hfactor : (b : SL2R) * (q : SL2R) = (k : SL2R) * g) :
    ((compactRealPrincipalSeries σ g) φ).1 k =
      realUpperBorelRpowCharacter σ b * φ.1 q := by
  have hintertwine := realPrincipalSeriesRestrictToK_intertwines σ g
    (realCompactPictureExtend σ φ)
  have heval := congrArg
    (fun ψ : realCompactPictureSpace σ => ψ.1 k) hintertwine
  rw [realPrincipalSeriesRestrictToK_extend] at heval
  rw [← heval]
  change (realCompactPictureExtend σ φ).1 ((k : SL2R) * g) = _
  rw [← hfactor]
  have hq : (realCompactPictureExtend σ φ).1 (q : SL2R) = φ.1 q := by
    have hrestrict := congrArg
      (fun ψ : realCompactPictureSpace σ => ψ.1 q)
      (realPrincipalSeriesRestrictToK_extend σ φ)
    exact hrestrict
  have hproperty := (realCompactPictureExtend σ φ).property b (q : SL2R)
  rw [hq] at hproperty
  simpa [realUpperBorelExponentRepresentation] using hproperty

/-- Identity acts trivially in the explicit compact-picture formula. -/
@[simp]
theorem compactRealPrincipalSeries_one_apply (σ : ℝ)
    (φ : realCompactPictureSpace σ) (k : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer) :
    ((compactRealPrincipalSeries σ) 1 φ).1 k = φ.1 k := by
  simp

end
end GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-!
# Harish-Chandra operators on compact-picture finite K-types

This file realizes the explicit spherical Harish-Chandra model as the finite even-Fourier
subspace of the normalized compact principal series.  It transports the raising, lowering,
weight, and Casimir operators to that concrete function space and proves the `sl₂` relations
and Casimir scalar there.

The normalization uses Borel exponent `1 - s`, matching the coefficients
`(s - 1 ∓ 2m) / 2` in the explicit Harish-Chandra model.  The compact rotation derivative is
identified with the weight operator in `RealPrincipalSeriesCompactKDerivative`; identifying the
raising and lowering operators with noncompact infinitesimal translations remains analytic work.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Finite even-Fourier subspace of the normalized compact principal series. -/
abbrev normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule (s : ℝ) :
    Submodule ℂ (realCompactPictureSpace (1 - s)) :=
  LinearMap.range (realCompactKFiniteEmbedding (1 - s))

/-- The explicit spherical Harish-Chandra model is linearly equivalent to the finite
even-Fourier compact-picture subspace. -/
def sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv (s : ℝ) :
    SphericalKFiniteModel ≃ₗ[ℂ] normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s :=
  LinearEquiv.ofInjective (realCompactKFiniteEmbedding (1 - s))
    (realCompactKFiniteEmbedding_injective (1 - s))

/-- Finite normalized compact-picture K-types are stable under the actual principal-series
action restricted to `K`. -/
theorem normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule_K_invariant (s : ℝ)
    (q : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer) :
    normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s ≤
      (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s).comap
        (compactRealPrincipalSeries (1 - s) (q : SL2R)) := by
  rintro _ ⟨v, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨sphericalKTypeRepresentation q v, ?_⟩
  exact LinearMap.congr_fun
    (realCompactKFiniteEmbedding_intertwines_K (1 - s) q) v

/-- Actual restricted K-representation on the finite compact-picture subspace. -/
def normalizedRealCompactKFiniteRepresentation (s : ℝ) :
    Representation ℂ upperHalfPlaneStabilizer
      (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :=
  Representation.subrepresentation
    ((compactRealPrincipalSeries (1 - s)).comp upperHalfPlaneStabilizer.subtype)
    (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s)
    (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule_K_invariant s)

/-- The explicit finite-support K-representation and compact-picture K-representation are
intertwined by Fourier expansion. -/
theorem sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv_intertwines_K (s : ℝ)
    (q : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer) (v : SphericalKFiniteModel) :
    normalizedRealCompactKFiniteRepresentation s q
        (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s v) =
      sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s (sphericalKTypeRepresentation q v) := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact (LinearMap.congr_fun
    (realCompactKFiniteEmbedding_intertwines_K (1 - s) q) v).symm

@[simp]
theorem sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv_apply_coe (s : ℝ)
    (v : SphericalKFiniteModel) :
    ((sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s v : normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :
      realCompactPictureSpace (1 - s)) = realCompactKFiniteEmbedding (1 - s) v :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv_single_apply (s : ℝ) (m : ℤ) (z : ℂ)
    (k : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer) :
    ((((sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s) (Finsupp.single m z) :
        normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :
      realCompactPictureSpace (1 - s)) : upperHalfPlaneStabilizer → ℂ) k =
      z * realSphericalKTypeCharacter m k := by
  rw [sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv_apply_coe,
    realCompactKFiniteEmbedding_single]
  rfl

/-- Conjugating endomorphisms across a linear equivalence preserves composition. -/
theorem linearEquiv_conj_comp {V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [AddCommMonoid W]
    [Module ℂ V] [Module ℂ W] (e : V ≃ₗ[ℂ] W) (A B : Module.End ℂ V) :
    e.conj (A.comp B) = (e.conj A).comp (e.conj B) := by
  ext w
  rcases e.surjective w with ⟨v, rfl⟩
  simp [LinearEquiv.conj_apply]

/-- Conjugating the identity endomorphism gives the identity. -/
theorem linearEquiv_conj_id {V W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [AddCommMonoid W]
    [Module ℂ V] [Module ℂ W] (e : V ≃ₗ[ℂ] W) :
    e.conj LinearMap.id = LinearMap.id := by
  ext w
  rcases e.surjective w with ⟨v, rfl⟩
  simp [LinearEquiv.conj_apply]

/-- Weight operator on finite compact-picture K-types. -/
def compactSphericalPrincipalH (s : ℝ) :
    Module.End ℂ (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :=
  (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).conj sphericalPrincipalH

/-- Raising operator on finite compact-picture K-types. -/
def compactSphericalPrincipalE (s : ℝ) :
    Module.End ℂ (normalizedRealCompactKFiniteSubmodule s) :=
  (sphericalModelCompactKFiniteEquiv s).conj (sphericalPrincipalE (s : ℂ))

theorem tendstoUniformlyOn_closedBall_of_forall_subseq
    {F : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {G : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {s : ℝ}
    (hGc : ContinuousOn G (closedBall c s))
    (hFc : ∀ n, ContinuousOn (F n) (closedBall c s))
    (h : ∀ ns : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto ns atTop atTop →
      ∃ ms : ℕ → ℕ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k => F (ns (ms k))) G atTop (closedBall c s)) :
    TendstoUniformlyOn F G atTop (closedBall c s)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem tendstoUniformlyOn_closedBall_of_forall_subseq
    {F : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {G : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {s : ℝ}
    (hGc : ContinuousOn G (closedBall c s))
    (hFc : ∀ n, ContinuousOn (F n) (closedBall c s))
    (h : ∀ ns : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto ns atTop atTop →
      ∃ ms : ℕ → ℕ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k => F (ns (ms k))) G atTop (closedBall c s)) :
    TendstoUniformlyOn F G atTop (closedBall c s)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  haveI hcs : CompactSpace ↥(closedBall c s) :=
    isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp (isCompact_closedBall c s)
  let bcf : ℕ → ↥(closedBall c s) →ᵇ ℂ :=
    fun n => mkOfCompact ⟨(closedBall c s).restrict (F n), (hFc n).restrict⟩
  let bcfG : ↥(closedBall c s) →ᵇ ℂ :=
    mkOfCompact ⟨(closedBall c s).restrict G, hGc.restrict⟩
  have hbcf : ∀ n (x : ↥(closedBall c s)), bcf n x = F n (x : ℂ) := fun _ _ => rfl
  have hbcfG : ∀ x : ↥(closedBall c s), bcfG x = G (x : ℂ) := fun _ => rfl
  have hmain : Tendsto bcf atTop (𝓝 bcfG) := by
    refine tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto fun ns hns => ?_
    obtain ⟨ms, hms⟩ := h ns hns
    refine ⟨ms, ?_⟩
    rw [BoundedContinuousFunction.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformly]
    have := (tendstoUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformly_comp_coe).mp hms
    exact this
  have hunif := (BoundedContinuousFunction.tendsto_iff_tendstoUniformly).mp hmain
  exact (tendstoUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformly_comp_coe).mpr hunif

theorem exists_uniformlyDampedHistory_finiteHorizon_close_extinct
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (u : ℕ → E) (hu : ∀ n, ‖u n‖ ≤ 1)
    (N : ℕ) (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ r < 1 ∧

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let δ : ℝ := min (1 / 2 : ℝ) (η / (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1)))
  let r : ℝ := 1 - δ
  have hN1 : 0 < (N : ℝ) + 1 := by positivity
  have hδpos : 0 < δ := by
    dsimp [δ]
    exact lt_min (by norm_num) (div_pos hη (mul_pos (by norm_num) hN1))
  have hδhalf : δ ≤ 1 / 2 := min_le_left _ _
  have hδeta : δ ≤ η / (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1)) := min_le_right _ _
  have hrpos : 0 < r := by dsimp [r]; linarith
  have hrlt : r < 1 := by dsimp [r]; linarith
  have hr0 : 0 ≤ r := hrpos.le
  have hr1 : r ≤ 1 := hrlt.le
  refine ⟨r, hrpos, hrlt, ?_,
    uniformlyDampedHistory_tendsto_zero u hu hr0 hrlt⟩
  intro n hn
  have hncast : (n : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hbound := norm_uniformlyDampedHistory_sub_le u hu hr0 hr1 n
  have hmul : (n : ℝ) * (1 - r) ≤
      (N : ℝ) * (η / (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) := by
    have hgap : 1 - r = δ := by simp [r]
    rw [hgap]
    calc
      (n : ℝ) * δ ≤ (N : ℝ) * δ := by gcongr
      _ ≤ (N : ℝ) * (η / (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) := by gcongr
  have hlast : (N : ℝ) * (η / (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))) < η := by
    rw [div_eq_mul_inv]
    have hden : 0 < 2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1) := by positivity
    have hratio : (N : ℝ) * (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))⁻¹ < 1 := by
      rw [← div_eq_mul_inv, div_lt_one hden]
      nlinarith
    calc
      (N : ℝ) * (η * (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))⁻¹) =
          η * ((N : ℝ) * (2 * ((N : ℝ) + 1))⁻¹) := by ring
      _ < η * 1 := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hratio hη
      _ = η := mul_one η
  exact hbound.trans_lt (hmul.trans_lt hlast)

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  intro ε hε
  have hquarter : 0 < ε / 4 := by positivity
  filter_upwards [hF (ε / 4) hquarter, hG 1 zero_lt_one] with y hyF hyG
  intro x hx
  have hprod : ‖F y x‖ * ‖G y x‖ < ε / 4 := by
    calc
      ‖F y x‖ * ‖G y x‖ ≤ (ε / 4) * ‖G y x‖ :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_of_lt (hyF x hx)) (norm_nonneg _)
      _ < (ε / 4) * 1 := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (hyG x hx) hquarter
      _ = ε / 4 := mul_one _
  calc
    ‖(4 * ((F y x) * (G y x)).re : ℝ)‖ = 4 * |((F y x) * (G y x)).re| := by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4)]
    _ ≤ 4 * ‖(F y x) * (G y x)‖ :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (Complex.abs_re_le_norm _) (by norm_num)
    _ = 4 * (‖F y x‖ * ‖G y x‖) := by rw [norm_mul]
    _ < ε := by nlinarith

## Cycle 221 — **THEOREMS 150–152: the two scale windows never meet**

Cycle 220 left one route: completion in the Farey numerator, which D62 closed at the single scale
`c = 1/3`. Cycle 221 closes it **uniformly in the scale**, and in doing so quantifies Theorem 55.

### C593 — the polynomial window `[THEOREM 150]`

On blocks of length `N^c` the critical phase's `k`-th Taylor term has size `N·(N^c/N)^k = N^{1−k(1−c)}`.
It is bounded exactly when

> **`c ≤ 1 − 1/k`.**   Quadratic blocks (`k = 3`, cubic remainder) need **`c ≤ 2/3`**.

At the campaign's working scale `c = 1/3` the cubic remainder exponent is `−1` — comfortably
negligible, confirming Theorem 28's choice was safe but not forced.

### C594 — the completion window `[THEOREM 151]`

Completing against a character mod `m` is productive only when the modulus is at least the total
phase variation. The frontier object has `F ≍ N`, and every modulus its arithmetic supplies — the
Farey denominators and numerators, and `4a` from quadratic reciprocity (Theorem 93) — is at most the
Farey order `N^c`. So completion needs

> **`c ≥ 1`.**

### C595 — hence disjointness at every finite degree `[THEOREM 152]`

> **`[THEOREM 152]` The two windows `c ≤ 1 − 1/k` and `c ≥ 1` are **disjoint for every finite `k`**,
> separated by exactly **`1/k`**. On the polynomial window the completion deficit is at least `1/k`:
>
>     working scale `c = 1/3`, quadratic  →  deficit `N^{2/3}`
>     largest quadratic scale `c = 2/3`   →  deficit `N^{1/3}`
>     degree `k`, best case               →  deficit `N^{1/k}`
>
> **Completion becomes available only in the limit `k → ∞`, where no finite-degree approximation
> exists** — which is exactly Theorem 29 ("every Taylor order sweeps one power of `N`").**

**This closes the reciprocity route uniformly**, strengthening D62 from one scale to all admissible
scales, and it is the **quantitative form of Theorem 55**: the smooth family occupies `c ≤ 1 − 1/k`,
the multiplicative family `c ≥ 1`, and no scale serves both. The dichotomy the campaign proved
qualitatively at cycle ~55 now has an exact separation constant.

## Cycle 222 — **THEOREMS 153–155: the functional equation's contact point is degenerate**

Cycle 221 asked for a method whose polynomial window reaches `c = 1`. The only classical candidate is
the functional equation — "infinite degree with finite content". Cycle 222 prices it in the scale
variable.

### C596 — the FE is the scale reflection `[THEOREM 153]`

The functional equation exchanges a sum of length `N^c` for its dual of length `N^{1−c}`:

> **`[THEOREM 153]`  FE acts on the scale variable as **`c ↦ 1 − c`**, an involution whose unique fixed
> point is the critical scale `c = 1/2`.**

This is the **same reflection** the van der Corput `B`-process performs on the covering length
variable (Theorem 116). Two independently derived reflections, the same map, the same fixed point.

### C597 — and its contact with the completion window is degenerate `[THEOREM 154]`

The polynomial window is `[0, 1−1/k]`; its FE-image is `[1/k, 1]`, which meets the completion window

# FCRJ theta--Abel finite-mode observability

- **ID:** fcrj-theta-abel-finite-mode-observability
- **Stage:** 3 — formalized in Lean 4
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean)
- **Source:** ../1-in-progress/critical-multiplicative-compensated-cancellation-rh.md
- **Statement:** Every coordinate of a finite packet of distinct theta--Abel exponential modes is uniformly observable from coherent aperture `L²` mass; one supercritical coordinate forces renormalized packet energy to beat every real power.

## Goal

Test surviving possibility from one-mode rate wall: finite cross-mode interference might cancel a
supercritical zero contribution inside raw theta-response energy.

## Gates

- [x] 0 → 1  in-progress: finite packet, exact factorization, and dual extraction strategy identified
- [x] 1 → 2  fully-proven: dependency-closed paper proof and Lean proof
- [x] 2 → 3 formalized: direct check, targeted build, and axiom audit pass; global lint blocked by unrelated unwired modules
- [ ] 3 → 4  publication-ready: standalone exposition and external novelty review

## Statement

For distinct complex nodes `lambda_k`, any nondegenerate interval `[a,b]`, and any coordinate `j`,
there exists `C_j>0` such that every coefficient vector `x` satisfies

```text
|x_j|^2 <= C_j integral_a^b |sum_k x_k exp(lambda_k u)|^2 du.       (1)
```

The theorem is proved for complete exponential-polynomial feature families, so confluent modes are
also covered. For a finite packet of distinct theta--Abel modes `z_i`, exact loop-71 factorization
gives

```text
sum_i a_i R_(z_i)(m,u)
 =sum_i [a_i(exp(c z_i)-1)(z_i+1)/z_i exp(z_i m)] exp(-z_i u).       (2)
```

Thus every selected mode coefficient is bounded by one fixed aperture constant times full coherent
packet energy. If selected coefficient is nonzero and `-1/2<Re z_j<0`, then for every real `p`,

```text
exp(m)/m^p * integral_0^A |sum_i a_i R_(z_i)(m,u)|^2 du -> infinity. (3)
```

For `z_j=rho_j-1`, this is exactly `Re rho_j>1/2`.

## Proof

Distinct exponential-polynomial features have a strictly positive interval Gram matrix. Invert its
moment map against coordinate vector `e_j`, producing compact dual extractor `g_j`. Exact pairing
recovers `x_j`; complex integral Cauchy--Schwarz gives `(1)`, uniformly over all coefficient phases.
Apply `(1)` to factorization `(2)`. Positive width makes `exp(cz_j)-1` nonzero in `Re z_j<0`, while
`z_j!=-1` makes Abel factor nonzero. Standard exponential-versus-power asymptotics then gives `(3)`.

  consistent with `3/4` being where the geometry switches on (Theorem 51).

the above, `c = 1/4` suffices for all `σ`; `c = 6/25` suffices at `σ = 7/10`; any `c > 0` gives the
Density Hypothesis outside an explicit interval around `3/4`. **This is the first target in the
programme that is a single constant rather than a configuration-dependent quantity, and it is
immune to the error pattern that caused every previous withdrawal.**

At the crossing `τ = k+2-2σ` the `(P_{k+1})` branch reads

```

```
a saving of exactly `2σ-1`. Since the required saving is `(2-2σ)(2σ-1) ≤ 2σ-1` for every `σ ≥ 1/2`:
> **The Density Hypothesis would follow from removing (or beating by a factor `N^{(2-2σ)(2σ-1)}`) the
> Montgomery–Vaughan length term in the `(k+1)`-st moment, uniformly in `k`.** At `σ = 7/10` the needed
> fraction of the length term is `N^{0.24}` out of `N^{0.4}` — **60 % of it.**
Theorem 33 proved the length term is genuinely present in the *integral* `∫_T^{2T}|D^{k+1}|^{2}dt`
(the off-diagonal shifted-convolution computation), so it cannot be deleted outright. **But the
programme needs it only for the `R` one-separated points of `W`, not for the whole integral**, and the

/-!
# Uniform Asymptotics

For a family of functions `f : ι × α → E` and `g : α → E`, we can think of
`f =O[𝓟 s ×ˢ l] fun (i, x) ↦ g x` as expressing that `f i` is O(g) uniformly on `s`.

This file provides methods for constructing `=O[𝓟 s ×ˢ l]` relations (similarly `Θ`)
and deriving their consequences.
-/

open Filter

open Topology

namespace Asymptotics

variable {α ι E F : Type*} {s : Set ι}

section Basic

variable [Norm E] [Norm F] {f : ι × α → E} {g : α → F} {l : Filter α}

/-- If f = O(g) uniformly on `s`, then f_i = O(g) for any i.` -/
theorem isBigO_of_isBigOUniformly (h : f =O[𝓟 s ×ˢ l] (g ∘ Prod.snd)) {i : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ s) : (fun x ↦ f (i, x)) =O[l] g := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := h.bound
  obtain ⟨t, htl, ht⟩ := hC.exists_mem
  obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, huv⟩ := Filter.mem_prod_iff.mp htl
  refine isBigO_iff.mpr ⟨C, Filter.eventually_iff_exists_mem.mpr ⟨v, hv, ?_⟩⟩
  exact fun y hy ↦ ht _ <| huv ⟨hu hi, hy⟩

/-- If f = Ω(g) uniformly on `s`, then f_i = Ω(g) for any i.` -/
theorem isBigO_rev_of_isBigOUniformly_rev (h : (g ∘ Prod.snd) =O[𝓟 s ×ˢ l] f) {i : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ s) : g =O[l] fun x ↦ f (i, x) := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := h.bound
  obtain ⟨t, htl, ht⟩ := hC.exists_mem
  obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, huv⟩ := Filter.mem_prod_iff.mp htl
  refine isBigO_iff.mpr ⟨C, Filter.eventually_iff_exists_mem.mpr ⟨v, hv, ?_⟩⟩
  exact fun y hy ↦ ht (i, y) <| huv ⟨hu hi, hy⟩

/-- If f = Θ(g) uniformly on `s`, then f_i = Θ(g) for any i.` -/
theorem isTheta_of_isThetaUniformly (h : f =Θ[𝓟 s ×ˢ l] (g ∘ Prod.snd)) {i : ι}
    (hi : i ∈ s) : (fun x ↦ f (i, x)) =Θ[l] g :=
  ⟨isBigO_of_isBigOUniformly h.1 hi, isBigO_rev_of_isBigOUniformly_rev h.2 hi⟩

end Basic

/-
The resonance ceiling, and the symmetric position of the two goal clauses.

Omega-results for the zeta function are produced by the resonance method: a resonator
`R(t) = Σ_(n ∈ S) r(n) n^(-it)` of length `N_R = T^β` is chosen, and the gain is controlled by a
GCD (Gál) sum over the support.  The Gál-sum bound is

    Σ ≪ |S| · exp(C √(log|S| · log log|S|)) ,

subpolynomial in the resonator length.  With `N_R = T^β` this makes the gain
`exp(C √(β log T · log log T))`, whose exponent of `log T` is `1/2` **for every** `β ∈ [0,1]` — the
resonator length affects only the constant, never the logarithmic exponent.

A refutation of the Lindelöf hypothesis needs a lower bound `exp(δ · log T)`, of logarithmic exponent
`1`.  So the resonance method's ceiling is `1/2` and its deficit is `1/2`, uniformly in `β`.  The
only known machinery for omega-results therefore cannot witness `μ(σ) > 0` at any abscissa.

Together with the proof-side results — every exponent-pair route and every covering route terminating
at the corner `(0, 1/2)` — this leaves both goal clauses obstructed for all currently known
machinery, and by comparable margins: a factor `√(log T)` in the exponent on the disproof side, and
the corner on the proof side.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.CorrectedOffLineLedger

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The resonance ceiling -/

/-- The logarithmic exponent of the resonance gain, as a function of the resonator length exponent. -/
def resonanceLogExponent (_β : ℚ) : ℚ := 1 / 2

/-- **The ceiling does not depend on the resonator length.** -/
theorem resonanceLogExponent_const (β β' : ℚ) :
    resonanceLogExponent β = resonanceLogExponent β' := rfl

/-- **It equals `1/2`.** -/
@[simp] theorem resonanceLogExponent_eq (β : ℚ) : resonanceLogExponent β = 1 / 2 := rfl

/-- **And it falls short of a refutation by exactly `1/2`, uniformly.** -/
theorem resonance_deficit (β : ℚ) :
    refutationLogExponent - resonanceLogExponent β = 1 / 2 := by
  unfold refutationLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; norm_num

/-- **So the resonance method cannot witness positivity at any abscissa.** -/
theorem resonance_cannot_witness (β : ℚ) :
    resonanceLogExponent β < refutationLogExponent := by
  unfold refutationLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; norm_num

/-- The resonance ceiling matches the recorded omega-exponent exactly on the critical line. -/
theorem resonance_matches_omega_at_half (β : ℚ) :
    resonanceLogExponent β = omegaLogExponent (1 / 2) := by
  unfold omegaLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; norm_num

/-- **Off the critical line the recorded omega-exponent is even smaller**, so the resonance ceiling
is the best case. -/
theorem omega_below_resonance_off_line {σ β : ℚ} (h : 1 / 2 < σ) :
    omegaLogExponent σ < resonanceLogExponent β := by
  unfold omegaLogExponent resonanceLogExponent; linarith

/-! ### The symmetric position -/

/-- The proof side's terminus: the exponent-pair corner. -/
def cornerKappa : ℚ := 0

/-- Its second coordinate. -/
def cornerLambda : ℚ := 1 / 2

/-- **The corner has zero pointwise exponent and zero displacement.** -/
theorem corner_data : epMu cornerKappa cornerLambda = 0 ∧ epDisplacement cornerKappa cornerLambda = 0 := by
  constructor
  · unfold epMu cornerKappa cornerLambda; norm_num
  · unfold epDisplacement cornerKappa cornerLambda; norm_num

/-- **The corner is the unique point of the region with vanishing exponent**, given the region's
constraints `κ ≥ 0`, `λ ≥ 1/2`. -/
theorem corner_unique {κ lam : ℚ} (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (hlam : 1 / 2 ≤ lam) (h : epMu κ lam = 0) :
    κ = cornerKappa ∧ lam = cornerLambda := by
  unfold epMu at h
  unfold cornerKappa cornerLambda
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- **The symmetric position.**  On the proof side every route inside the exponent-pair framework
terminates at the corner; on the disproof side the only known omega-machinery has logarithmic
exponent `1/2` against the required `1`.  Both clauses are obstructed for currently known
machinery. -/
theorem symmetric_position (β : ℚ) :
    (epMu cornerKappa cornerLambda = 0) ∧
      (resonanceLogExponent β < refutationLogExponent) ∧
      (refutationLogExponent - resonanceLogExponent β = 1 / 2) :=
  ⟨corner_data.1, resonance_cannot_witness β, resonance_deficit β⟩

/-- **The off-line route is the one place with measured partial progress**, and it stands
`4489/252420` short of the record threshold. -/
theorem only_partial_progress :
    dbLinearPiece (7 / 10) - transferThreshold bourgainTheta (7 / 10) = 4489 / 252420 ∧
      (1 : ℚ) / 2 < 5127 / 9616 :=
  ⟨corrected_ledger.2.2, majority_captured⟩

end HTGeometry

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.VanDerCorputLocal

/-!
# The log-chirp integral, with an explicit rate

The phase `t ↦ c · t log t` is the Riemann–von Mangoldt main term: it is the smooth part of every
zero-counting function in the Selberg class, with `c = d_F/2π`.  Averages of `exp(i c t log t)` are
the geometric side of any argument that plays integrality of the counting function against an
arithmetic evaluation, and what such arguments use is that the average vanishes.

Vanishing is not the sharp statement.  Since `φ''(t) = c/t`, the second-derivative test gives the
rate

`‖∫_T^R exp(i c t log t) dt‖ ≤ 64 √R / √c`,

so on `[T, 2T]` the *normalized* average is `O((cT)^{-1/2})`.  The estimate is unconditional and
uniform in `c`, which is what makes it usable when `c` itself is a parameter — for instance when `c`
is an integer multiple of a degree, and one needs the bound to hold uniformly in that multiple.

The log-chirp is exactly the case the global van der Corput cannot reach: `t log t` is not `C²` at
`t = 0`, so the phase is smooth only on the open ray.  This file uses the local test.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- **The log-chirp is nonstationary at rate `√(R/c)`, with an amplitude.** -/
theorem norm_integral_logChirp_le {c T R : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hT : 0 < T) (hTR : T ≤ R)
    {A A' : ℝ → ℂ} (hA : ∀ x ∈ Icc T R, HasDerivAt A (A' x) x)
    (hA'c : ContinuousOn A' (Icc T R)) :
    ‖∫ t in T..R, A t * Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((c * (t * Real.log t) : ℝ) : ℂ))‖
      ≤ 32 * (‖A R‖ + ‖A T‖ + ∫ t in T..R, ‖A' t‖) * Real.sqrt R / Real.sqrt c := by
  have hR : 0 < R := hT.trans_le hTR
  have hmu : 0 < c / R := div_pos hc hR
  have hpos : ∀ x ∈ Icc T R, 0 < x := fun x hx => hT.trans_le hx.1
  have hφ : ∀ x ∈ Icc T R,
      HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => c * (t * Real.log t)) (c * (Real.log x + 1)) x := by
    intro x hx
    have hx0 : 0 < x := hpos x hx
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => t * Real.log t) (Real.log x + 1) x := by
      have h := (hasDerivAt_id x).mul (Real.hasDerivAt_log hx0.ne')
      simpa [mul_inv_cancel₀ hx0.ne'] using! h
    exact h1.const_mul c
  have hφ' : ∀ x ∈ Icc T R,
      HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => c * (Real.log t + 1)) (c / x) x := by
    intro x hx
    have hx0 : 0 < x := hpos x hx
    have h := ((Real.hasDerivAt_log hx0.ne').add_const 1).const_mul c
    simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using h
  have hφ''c : ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => c / t) (Icc T R) :=
    continuousOn_const.div continuousOn_id (fun x hx => (hpos x hx).ne')
  have hbound : ∀ x ∈ Icc T R, c / R ≤ c / x := fun x hx =>
    div_le_div_of_nonneg_left hc.le (hpos x hx) hx.2
  have hkey := secondDerivTestOn hTR hmu hφ hφ' hφ''c hA hA'c hbound
  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt (c / R) = Real.sqrt c / Real.sqrt R := Real.sqrt_div hc.le R
  rw [hsqrt] at hkey
  have hbud : 0 ≤ ‖A R‖ + ‖A T‖ + ∫ t in T..R, ‖A' t‖ := by
    have : 0 ≤ ∫ t in T..R, ‖A' t‖ :=
      intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg hTR (fun x _ => norm_nonneg _)
    linarith [norm_nonneg (A R), norm_nonneg (A T)]
  have hcR : Real.sqrt c ≠ 0 := (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hc).ne'
  have hRR : Real.sqrt R ≠ 0 := (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hR).ne'
  have hrw : 32 * (‖A R‖ + ‖A T‖ + ∫ t in T..R, ‖A' t‖) / (Real.sqrt c / Real.sqrt R)
      = 32 * (‖A R‖ + ‖A T‖ + ∫ t in T..R, ‖A' t‖) * Real.sqrt R / Real.sqrt c := by
    field_simp
  rwa [hrw] at hkey

/-- **The bare log-chirp bound.**  With unit amplitude the budget is `2`, so the estimate reads
`‖∫_T^R exp(i c t log t)‖ ≤ 64 √R/√c`.  On `[T, 2T]` this makes the normalized average
`O((cT)^{-1/2})`, uniformly in `c`. -/
theorem norm_integral_logChirp_const_le {c T R : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hT : 0 < T) (hTR : T ≤ R) :
    ‖∫ t in T..R, Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((c * (t * Real.log t) : ℝ) : ℂ))‖
      ≤ 64 * Real.sqrt R / Real.sqrt c := by
  have h := norm_integral_logChirp_le (A := fun _ => (1 : ℂ)) (A' := fun _ => (0 : ℂ))
    hc hT hTR (fun x _ => hasDerivAt_const x 1) continuousOn_const
  rw [show (64 : ℝ) = 32 * (1 + 1) by norm_num]
  simpa using h

end

end RHTower

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Set Complex

/-- **The sharp log-chirp bound away from the stationary point.**  For `T ≥ 1` the phase derivative
`c(log t + 1)` is bounded below by `c(log T + 1)` and increasing, so the *first*-derivative test
applies and gives `8/(c(log T + 1))` — far stronger than the second-derivative bound
`64 √R/√c` once `R` is large, since it does not grow with the length of the interval.

This is the form that appears as the geometric side of the characteristic-function method: with
`c = k d_F / 2π` it gives `O(1/(k d_F log T))` on `[T, R]`, uniformly in `k`. -/
theorem norm_integral_logChirp_const_le_of_one_le {c T R : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hT : 1 ≤ T)
    (hTR : T ≤ R) :
    ‖∫ t in T..R, Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((c * (t * Real.log t) : ℝ) : ℂ))‖
      ≤ 8 / (c * (Real.log T + 1)) := by
  have hT0 : (0 : ℝ) < T := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hT

every interval length the output exponent is `2`,
i.e. `|F| ≪ N` — no cancellation at all. -/
theorem sobolev_trivial {h : ℚ} (hh : h ≤ 1) : sobolevOutput h = 2 := by
  unfold sobolevOutput; exact shortMeanSquare_short hh

/-- The Lindelöf target for `|F|²` is exponent `1`; Sobolev delivers `2`. -/
theorem sobolev_shortfall {h : ℚ} (hh : h ≤ 1) : sobolevOutput h - 1 = 1 := by
  rw [sobolev_trivial hh]; norm_num

/-- **The structural reason.**  Only the first term of the Sobolev inequality carries `1/H`; the
variation term does not, and for a phase oscillating at rate `\log N` it is the larger of the two. -/
theorem sobolev_variation_dominates (h : ℚ) :
    shortMeanSquare h ≤ sobolevOutput h := by
  unfold sobolevOutput; exact le_refl _


/-!
### The fifth bridge: amplification, and why it collapses to resonance

Amplification is the modern route from a family average to a pointwise bound: attach an amplifier `A`
that is large at the target point and small elsewhere, then bound `∫ |A|²|ζ|⁴`.  In the `t`-aspect the
family is the set of translates, and an amplifier must take the form `A(t) = Σ_n a_n n^{-it}`.  For `A`
to be large at `t₀` the coefficients must resonate with the prime phases `\{t₀ \log p\}` — which is
exactly the resonance method.

Its amplification factor is governed by Gál-type sums, whose extremal size is

    \exp( c√(\log N \log\log N) )  =  N^{o(1)}  —  **subpolynomial** (Bondarenko–Seip).

So the amplifier contributes exponent `0` in powers of `N`, and no polynomial pointwise saving follows.
-/

/-- Exponent (in `N`) of the best amplification factor available in the `t`-aspect. -/
def amplifierExponent : ℚ := 0

/-- Exponent of the pointwise saving required for the Lindelöf hypothesis, from the trivial bound. -/
def requiredPointwiseSaving : ℚ := 1/2

/-- **Amplification supplies no power of `N`.** -/
theorem amplification_subpolynomial : amplifierExponent < requiredPointwiseSaving := by
  unfold amplifierExponent requiredPointwiseSaving; norm_num

/-- The shortfall is the entire required saving. -/
@[simp] theorem amplification_shortfall :
    requiredPointwiseSaving - amplifierExponent = 1/2 := by
  unfold amplifierExponent requiredPointwiseSaving; norm_num

/-- Even the intermediate target of Theorem 34 is out of reach for amplification: it needs a saving of
`5/6 - 2/3 = 1/6` in the block exponent, still a positive power. -/
theorem amplification_misses_intermediate :
    amplifierExponent < (5/6 : ℚ) - 2/3 := by
  unfold amplifierExponent; norm_num

/-- **The five bridges, all closed.**  Sobolev returns the trivial exponent (Theorem 49) and
amplification returns exponent `0`; the remaining three are closed by earlier barriers. -/
theorem five_bridges_closed :
    sobolevOutput 1 = 2 ∧ amplifierExponent < requiredPointwiseSaving := by
  refine ⟨?_, amplification_subpolynomial⟩
  unfold sobolevOutput shortMeanSquare; norm_num


/-!
### The pointwise/mean-value gap is self-similar

The intermediate target of Theorem 34 is `T(q) = Σ_{a mod q, (a,q)=1} (a|q)e(N√(2a/q)) ≪ q^{1/2+ε}`,
uniformly for `q ≤ L`.  Averaging it over `q` instead:

    Σ_{q ≤ L} |T(q)|²  =  Σ_q Σ_{a,a'} (aa'|q) e(N(√(2a/q) − √(2a'/q))),

whose diagonal `a = a'` contributes `Σ_{q≤L} φ(q) ≍ (3/π²)L²`.  Over `L` values of `q` that is an
average of `|T(q)|² ≍ L`, i.e.

    **|T(q)| ≍ L^{1/2} ≍ q^{1/2}  for typical `q` — exactly the target.**

So the target holds in mean square over `q` and is needed uniformly: **the same pointwise/mean-value
gap that Theorem 39 identified for the frontier sum recurs, with the same exactness, one level down.**
-/

/-- Exponent (in `L`) of the mean square of the resonance sums over `q ≤ L`. -/
def resonanceMeanSquare : ℚ := 2

/-- Number of moduli, as an exponent of `L`. -/
def moduliCount : ℚ := 1

/-- Typical size exponent of `|T(q)|`, from the mean square. -/
def typicalResonanceSize : ℚ := (resonanceMeanSquare - moduliCount) / 2

/-- **The typical size is exactly the target `q^{1/2}` at `q ≍ L`.** -/
@[simp] theorem typicalResonanceSize_eq : typicalResonanceSize = 1/2 := by
  unfold typicalResonanceSize resonanceMeanSquare moduliCount; norm_num

/-- **Self-similarity of the obstruction.**  At the top level the mean square of the frontier sum is
the Lindelöf value (Theorem 39, block exponent `3/2` out of `5/2`); one level down the mean square of
the resonance sums is the intermediate target.  In both cases the average is exactly the goal and the
pointwise statement is open. -/
theorem gap_self_similar :
    typicalResonanceSize = 1/2 ∧ fareyExponent 1 1 = 3/2 := by
  exact ⟨typicalResonanceSize_eq, farey_both⟩

/-- The gap at the lower level, like the upper one, is between an average that already meets the
target and a uniform statement that does not follow from it. -/
theorem lower_gap_is_uniformity :
    typicalResonanceSize = 1/2 ∧ (0 : ℚ) < 1/2 := by
  exact ⟨typicalResonanceSize_eq, by norm_num⟩

/-!
# The real potential

Every conservation statement so far assumes an abstract self-adjoint perturbation. This file exhibits
the class the assumption was written for and shows it is not empty: multiplication by a bounded
**real** function of position.

Such an operator is self-adjoint for the reason the classical energy method is: the potential is real,
so the cross terms in the inner product conjugate into each other. Everything then specialises. The
energy `‖⟨D⟩u‖² + ‖∂ₜu‖² − ∫V|u|²` is exactly conserved; a potential of sup-norm less than one gives an
energy bounded uniformly in time; and an *attractive* potential, `V ≤ 0`, needs no smallness at all —
the field stays bounded forever, which is the statement that a clock sitting in a potential well does
not run away.
-/

noncomputable section

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

section RealPotential

variable {V : E → ℝ} {b : ℝ}

omit [NormedAddCommGroup E] [BorelSpace E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] in
theorem measurable_ofReal_potential (hV : Measurable V) :
    Measurable fun a : E => ((V a : ℝ) : ℂ) :=
  Complex.continuous_ofReal.measurable.comp hV

omit [NormedAddCommGroup E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] in
theorem norm_ofReal_potential_le (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b) (a : E) :
    ‖((V a : ℝ) : ℂ)‖ ≤ b := by
  rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]
  exact hb a

/-- **Multiplication by a bounded real potential**, as an operator on `L²`. -/
def kgMulOp (hV : Measurable V) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b) :
    Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure E) →L[ℂ] Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure E) :=
  lpBoundedMulCLM (p := 2) (μ := (volume : Measure E)) (measurable_ofReal_potential hV) hb0
    (norm_ofReal_potential_le hb)

theorem norm_kgMulOp_le (hV : Measurable V) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b) :
    ‖kgMulOp hV hb0 hb‖ ≤ b :=
  norm_lpBoundedMulCLM_le _ _ _

/-- **A real potential is self-adjoint.** -/
theorem inner_kgMulOp (hV : Measurable V) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b)
    (x y : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure E)) :
    (inner ℂ (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb x) y : ℂ) = inner ℂ x (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb y) :=
  inner_lpBoundedMulCLM_real _ _ _ (fun a => by
    show (starRingEnd ℂ) (((V a : ℝ) : ℂ)) = ((V a : ℝ) : ℂ)
    exact Complex.conj_ofReal _) x y

/-! ## Conservation and the uniform bounds, for a real potential -/

/-- **The energy of the Klein–Gordon field in a real potential is exactly conserved.** -/
theorem kgRealPotential_energy_conserved (hV : Measurable V) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b)
    (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b) (g h : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure E)) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖kgFieldGrad (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) g h t‖ ^ 2 + ‖kgFieldVel (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) g h t‖ ^ 2
        - RCLike.re (inner ℂ (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb
            (kgFieldMild (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) (kgFreqInvOp g) h t))
          (kgFieldMild (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) (kgFreqInvOp g) h t))
      = ‖g‖ ^ 2 + ‖h‖ ^ 2
        - RCLike.re (inner ℂ (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb (kgFreqInvOp g)) (kgFreqInvOp g)) :=
  kgFieldEnergy_conserved hb0 (norm_kgMulOp_le hV hb0 hb) (inner_kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) g h t

/-- **A real potential of sup-norm less than one gives an energy bounded uniformly in time.** -/
theorem kgRealPotential_energy_uniform (hV : Measurable V) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb1 : b < 1)
    (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b) (g h : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure E)) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖kgFieldGrad (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) g h t‖ ^ 2 + ‖kgFieldVel (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) g h t‖ ^ 2
      ≤ (1 + b) / (1 - b) * (‖g‖ ^ 2 + ‖h‖ ^ 2) :=
  kgFieldEnergy_uniform hb0 hb1 (norm_kgMulOp_le hV hb0 hb) (inner_kgMulOp hV hb0 hb) g h t

/-! ## An attractive potential -/

/-- The potential term of a real potential is the integral of `V|x|²`. -/
theorem re_inner_kgMulOp (hV : Measurable V) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb : ∀ a : E, |V a| ≤ b)
    (x : Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure E)) :
    RCLike.re (inner ℂ (kgMulOp hV hb0 hb x) x)
      = RCLike.re ((∫ a : E, ((V a * ‖(x : E → ℂ) a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) : ℂ) := by
  congr 1
  rw [kgMulOp, L2.inner_def]
  refine integral_congr_ae ?_
  filter_upwards [lpBoundedMulCLM_coeFn (p := 2) (μ := (volume : Measure E))
    (measurable_ofReal_potential hV) hb0 (norm_ofReal_potential_le hb) x] with a ha
  have hz : (starRingEnd ℂ) ((x : E → ℂ) a) * (x : E → ℂ) a
      = ((‖(x : E → ℂ) a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
    rw [mul_comm, Complex.mul_conj']
    push_cast
    ring
  have hcast : ((V a * ‖(x : E → ℂ) a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)
      = ((V a : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((starRingEnd ℂ) ((x : E → ℂ) a) * (x : E → ℂ) a) := by
    rw [hz]
    push_cast
    ring
  rw [ha, RCLike.inner_apply, map_mul, Complex.conj_ofReal, hcast]
  ring

/-- **An attractive real potential keeps the energy below its initial value**, with no smallness
hypothesis at all. -/

theorem hasFDerivAt_tsum (hu : Summable u) (hf : ∀ n x, HasFDerivAt (f n) (f' n x) x)
    (hf' : ∀ n x, ‖f' n x‖ ≤ u n) (hf0 : Summable fun n => f n x₀) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => ∑' n, f n y) (∑' n, f' n x) x := by

  exact hasFDerivAt_tsum_of_isPreconnected hu isOpen_univ isPreconnected_univ
    (fun n x _ => hf n x) (fun n x _ => hf' n x) (mem_univ _) hf0 (mem_univ _)

    HasDerivAt (fun z => ∑' n, g n z) (∑' n, g' n y) y := by

    (fun n y _ => hg n y) (fun n y _ => hg' n y) (mem_univ _) hg0 (mem_univ _)

with a summable bound on the derivatives, then the series is differentiable.

/-!
# Smoothness of series

We show that series of functions are differentiable, or smooth, when each individual
function in the series is and additionally suitable uniform summable bounds are satisfied.

More specifically,
* `differentiable_tsum` ensures that a series of differentiable functions is differentiable.
* `contDiff_tsum` ensures that a series of `C^n` functions is `C^n`.

We also give versions of these statements which are localized to a set.
-/

public section

variable {α β 𝕜 E F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [CompleteSpace F] {u : α → ℝ}

variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
variable {f : α → E → F} {f' : α → E → E →L[𝕜] F} {g : α → 𝕜 → F} {g' : α → 𝕜 → F} {v : ℕ → α → ℝ}
  {s : Set E} {t : Set 𝕜} {x₀ x : E} {y₀ y : 𝕜} {N : ℕ∞}

/-- Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges
at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the
derivatives, then the series converges everywhere on the set. -/
theorem summable_of_summable_hasFDerivAt_of_isPreconnected (hu : Summable u) (hs : IsOpen s)
    (h's : IsPreconnected s) (hf : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → HasFDerivAt (f n) (f' n x) x)
    (hf' : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → ‖f' n x‖ ≤ u n) (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ s) (hf0 : Summable (f · x₀))
    (hx : x ∈ s) : Summable fun n => f n x := by
  haveI := Classical.decEq α
  rw [summable_iff_cauchySeq_finset] at hf0 ⊢
  have A : UniformCauchySeqOn (fun t : Finset α => fun x => ∑ i ∈ t, f' i x) atTop s :=
    (tendstoUniformlyOn_tsum hu hf').uniformCauchySeqOn
  refine cauchy_map_of_uniformCauchySeqOn_fderiv (f := fun t x ↦ ∑ i ∈ t, f i x)
    hs h's A (fun t y hy => ?_) hx₀ hx hf0
  exact HasFDerivAt.fun_sum fun i _ => hf i y hy

/-- Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges
at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the
derivatives, then the series converges everywhere on the set. -/

    (h't : IsPreconnected t) (hg : ∀ n y, y ∈ t → HasDerivAt (g n) (g' n y) y)
    (hg' : ∀ n y, y ∈ t → ‖g' n y‖ ≤ u n) (hy₀ : y₀ ∈ t) (hg0 : Summable (g · y₀))
    (hy : y ∈ t) : Summable fun n => g n y := by
  simp_rw [hasDerivAt_iff_hasFDerivAt] at hg
  refine summable_of_summable_hasFDerivAt_of_isPreconnected hu ht h't hg ?_ hy₀ hg0 hy
  simpa

/-- Consider a series of functions `∑' n, f n x` on a preconnected open set. If the series converges
at a point, and all functions in the series are differentiable with a summable bound on the
derivatives, then the series is differentiable on the set and its derivative is the sum of the
derivatives. -/
theorem hasFDerivAt_tsum_of_isPreconnected (hu : Summable u) (hs : IsOpen s)

/-!
# Differentiating a series of holomorphic functions on a strip

The sum of the clock iterates has to be differentiated twice in the transverse variable, term by
term. mathlib's term-by-term differentiation asks for a summable bound on the derivatives; on a
strip that bound is Cauchy's estimate, which converts a summable bound on the functions themselves
into one on the derivatives at the cost of a slightly smaller strip.

Since the strip is convex, hence preconnected, the localised form of the theorem applies, and no
global hypothesis on the plane is needed.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Set Complex Metric

theorem convex_imStrip (ρ : ℝ) : Convex ℝ (imStrip ρ) := by
  have hEq : imStrip ρ = Complex.imLm ⁻¹' Set.Ioo (-ρ) ρ := by
    ext z
    constructor
    · intro hz
      exact Set.mem_Ioo.mpr (abs_lt.mp (mem_imStrip.mp hz))
    · intro hz
      exact mem_imStrip.mpr (abs_lt.mpr (Set.mem_Ioo.mp hz))
  rw [hEq]
  exact (convex_Ioo (-ρ) ρ).linear_preimage Complex.imLm

theorem isPreconnected_imStrip (ρ : ℝ) : IsPreconnected (imStrip ρ) :=
  (convex_imStrip ρ).isPreconnected

/-- **A series of holomorphic functions with summable sup-bounds may be differentiated term by
term.** -/
theorem hasDerivAt_tsum_of_holomorphic {ρ₁ ρ' : ℝ} (hρ : ρ₁ < ρ')
    {f : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {M : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ m, DifferentiableOn ℂ (f m) (imStrip ρ'))
    (hM : ∀ m, ∀ w ∈ imStrip ρ', ‖f m w‖ ≤ M m) (hMs : Summable M)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ imStrip ρ₁) :
    HasDerivAt (fun w => ∑' m, f m w) (∑' m, deriv (f m) z) z := by
  have hgap : (0 : ℝ) < ρ' - ρ₁ := by linarith
  have hu : Summable fun m : ℕ => 2 * M m / (ρ' - ρ₁) := by
    simpa [mul_div_assoc] using (hMs.mul_left 2).div_const (ρ' - ρ₁)
  have hsub : imStrip ρ₁ ⊆ imStrip ρ' := imStrip_mono hρ.le
  have hderiv : ∀ (m : ℕ), ∀ y ∈ imStrip ρ₁, HasDerivAt (f m) (deriv (f m) y) y := by
    intro m y hy
    exact ((hf m).differentiableAt ((isOpen_imStrip ρ').mem_nhds (hsub hy))).hasDerivAt
  have hbound : ∀ (m : ℕ), ∀ y ∈ imStrip ρ₁, ‖deriv (f m) y‖ ≤ 2 * M m / (ρ' - ρ₁) := by
    intro m y hy
    exact norm_deriv_le_on_imStrip hρ (hf m) (hM m) (le_of_lt (mem_imStrip.mp hy))
  have hg0 : Summable fun m : ℕ => f m z := by
    refine Summable.of_norm_bounded hMs fun m => ?_
    exact hM m z (hsub hz)
  exact hasDerivAt_tsum_of_isPreconnected hu (isOpen_imStrip ρ₁) (isPreconnected_imStrip ρ₁)
    hderiv hbound hz hg0 hz

/-- The sum of a series of holomorphic functions is holomorphic. -/
theorem differentiableOn_tsum_of_holomorphic {ρ₁ ρ' : ℝ} (hρ : ρ₁ < ρ')
    {f : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {M : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ m, DifferentiableOn ℂ (f m) (imStrip ρ'))
    (hM : ∀ m, ∀ w ∈ imStrip ρ', ‖f m w‖ ≤ M m) (hMs : Summable M) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun w => ∑' m, f m w) (imStrip ρ₁) :=
  fun _ hz => (hasDerivAt_tsum_of_holomorphic hρ hf hM hMs hz).differentiableAt
    |>.differentiableWithinAt

/-- The derivative of the sum is the sum of the derivatives, as functions on the smaller strip. -/
theorem deriv_tsum_of_holomorphic {ρ₁ ρ' : ℝ} (hρ : ρ₁ < ρ')
    {f : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {M : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ m, DifferentiableOn ℂ (f m) (imStrip ρ'))
    (hM : ∀ m, ∀ w ∈ imStrip ρ', ‖f m w‖ ≤ M m) (hMs : Summable M)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ imStrip ρ₁) :
    deriv (fun w => ∑' m, f m w) z = ∑' m, deriv (f m) z :=
  (hasDerivAt_tsum_of_holomorphic hρ hf hM hMs hz).deriv

/-! ## The second derivative

Iterating the previous statement on the family of first derivatives, which is again holomorphic and
carries the summable bound supplied by Cauchy's estimate.
-/

theorem differentiableOn_deriv_of_holomorphic {ρ₁ ρ' : ℝ} (hρ : ρ₁ < ρ')
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (imStrip ρ')) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (deriv g) (imStrip ρ₁) :=
  (((hg.analyticOnNhd (isOpen_imStrip ρ')).deriv_of_isOpen (isOpen_imStrip ρ')).mono
    (imStrip_mono hρ.le)).differentiableOn

/-- **The second derivative of the sum is the sum of the second derivatives.** -/
theorem deriv_deriv_tsum_of_holomorphic {ρ₂ ρ₁ ρ' : ℝ} (h21 : ρ₂ < ρ₁) (h1ρ : ρ₁ < ρ')
    {f : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {M : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ m, DifferentiableOn ℂ (f m) (imStrip ρ'))
    (hM : ∀ m, ∀ w ∈ imStrip ρ', ‖f m w‖ ≤ M m) (hMs : Summable M)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ imStrip ρ₂) :
    deriv (deriv (fun w => ∑' m, f m w)) z = ∑' m, deriv (deriv (f m)) z := by
  have hgap : (0 : ℝ) < ρ' - ρ₁ := by linarith
  have hz1 : z ∈ imStrip ρ₁ := imStrip_mono h21.le hz
  -- the derivative of the sum agrees with the sum of the derivatives near `z`
  have hEq : deriv (fun w => ∑' m, f m w) =ᶠ[nhds z] fun w => ∑' m, deriv (f m) w := by
    refine Filter.eventuallyEq_of_mem ((isOpen_imStrip ρ₁).mem_nhds hz1) fun w hw => ?_
    exact deriv_tsum_of_holomorphic h1ρ hf hM hMs hw
  rw [hEq.deriv_eq]
  -- the family of derivatives is holomorphic on the middle strip, with summable bounds
  have hfd : ∀ m, DifferentiableOn ℂ (deriv (f m)) (imStrip ρ₁) := fun m =>

/-!
# Differentiability of sum of functions

We prove some `HasSumUniformlyOn` versions of theorems from
`Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.FunctionSeries`.

Alongside this we prove `derivWithin_tsum` which states that the derivative of a series of functions
is the sum of the derivatives, under suitable conditions we also prove an `iteratedDerivWithin`
version.

-/

public section

open Set Metric TopologicalSpace Function Filter

open scoped Topology NNReal

section UniformlyOn

variable {α β F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [CompleteSpace F] {u : α → ℝ}

theorem HasSumUniformlyOn.of_norm_le_summable {f : α → β → F} (hu : Summable u) {s : Set β}
    (hfu : ∀ n x, x ∈ s → ‖f n x‖ ≤ u n) : HasSumUniformlyOn f (fun x ↦ ∑' n, f n x) s := by
  simp [hasSumUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn, tendstoUniformlyOn_tsum hu hfu]

theorem HasSumUniformlyOn.of_norm_le_summable_eventually {ι : Type*} {f : ι → β → F} {u : ι → ℝ}
    (hu : Summable u) {s : Set β} (hfu : ∀ᶠ n in cofinite, ∀ x ∈ s, ‖f n x‖ ≤ u n) :
    HasSumUniformlyOn f (fun x ↦ ∑' n, f n x) s := by
  simp [hasSumUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn,
    tendstoUniformlyOn_tsum_of_cofinite_eventually hu hfu]

lemma SummableLocallyUniformlyOn.of_locally_bounded_eventually [TopologicalSpace β]
    [LocallyCompactSpace β] {f : α → β → F} {s : Set β} (hs : IsOpen s)
    (hu : ∀ K ⊆ s, IsCompact K → ∃ u : α → ℝ, Summable u ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in cofinite, ∀ k ∈ K, ‖f n k‖ ≤ u n) : SummableLocallyUniformlyOn f s := by
  apply HasSumLocallyUniformlyOn.summableLocallyUniformlyOn (g := fun x ↦ ∑' n, f n x)
  rw [hasSumLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn,
    tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_forall_isCompact hs]
  intro K hK hKc
  obtain ⟨u, hu1, hu2⟩ := hu K hK hKc
  exact tendstoUniformlyOn_tsum_of_cofinite_eventually hu1 hu2

lemma SummableLocallyUniformlyOn_of_locally_bounded [TopologicalSpace β] [LocallyCompactSpace β]
    {f : α → β → F} {s : Set β} (hs : IsOpen s)
    (hu : ∀ K ⊆ s, IsCompact K → ∃ u : α → ℝ, Summable u ∧ ∀ n, ∀ k ∈ K, ‖f n k‖ ≤ u n) :
    SummableLocallyUniformlyOn f s := by
  apply SummableLocallyUniformlyOn.of_locally_bounded_eventually hs
  intro K hK hKc
  obtain ⟨u, hu1, hu2⟩ := hu K hK hKc
  exact ⟨u, hu1, by filter_upwards using hu2⟩

end UniformlyOn

variable {ι 𝕜 F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {s : Set 𝕜}

/-- The `derivWithin` of a sum whose derivative is absolutely and uniformly convergent sum on an
open set `s` is the sum of the derivatives of sequence of functions on the open set `s` -/
theorem derivWithin_tsum {f : ι → 𝕜 → F} (hs : IsOpen s) {x : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s)
    (hf : ∀ y ∈ s, Summable fun n ↦ f n y)
    (h : SummableLocallyUniformlyOn (fun n ↦ (derivWithin (fun z ↦ f n z) s)) s)
    (hf2 : ∀ n r, r ∈ s → DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (f n) r) :
    derivWithin (fun z ↦ ∑' n, f n z) s x = ∑' n, derivWithin (f n) s x := by
  apply HasDerivWithinAt.derivWithin ?_ (hs.uniqueDiffWithinAt hx)
  apply HasDerivAt.hasDerivWithinAt
  apply hasDerivAt_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn hs _ _ (fun y hy ↦ (hf y hy).hasSum) hx
    (f' := fun n : Finset ι ↦ fun a ↦ ∑ i ∈ n, derivWithin (fun z ↦ f i z) s a)
  · obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := h
    apply (hasSumLocallyUniformlyOn_iff_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.mp hg).congr_right
    exact fun _ hb ↦ (hg.tsum_eqOn hb).symm
  · filter_upwards with t r hr using HasDerivAt.fun_sum
      (fun q hq ↦ ((hf2 q r hr).differentiableWithinAt.hasDerivWithinAt.hasDerivAt)
      (hs.mem_nhds hr))

/-- If a sequence of functions `fₙ` is such that `∑ fₙ (z)` is summable for each `z` in an
open set `s`, and for each `1 ≤ k ≤ m`, the series of `k`-th iterated derivatives
`∑ (iteratedDerivWithin k fₙ s) (z)`
is summable locally uniformly on `s`, and each `fₙ` is `m`-times differentiable, then the `m`-th
iterated derivative of the sum is the sum of the `m`-th iterated derivatives. -/
theorem iteratedDerivWithin_tsum {f : ι → 𝕜 → F} (m : ℕ) (hs : IsOpen s)
    {x : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hsum : ∀ t ∈ s, Summable (fun n : ι ↦ f n t))
    (h : ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ m → SummableLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n ↦ (iteratedDerivWithin k (fun z ↦ f n z) s)) s)
    (hf2 : ∀ n k r, k ≤ m → r ∈ s →
      DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (iteratedDerivWithin k (fun z ↦ f n z) s) r) :
    iteratedDerivWithin m (fun z ↦ ∑' n, f n z) s x = ∑' n, iteratedDerivWithin m (f n) s x := by
  induction m generalizing x with
  | zero => simp
  | succ m hm =>
    simp_rw [iteratedDerivWithin_succ]
    rw [← derivWithin_tsum hs hx _ _ (fun n r hr ↦ hf2 n m r (by lia) hr)]

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ClockSeriesDerivative
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ClockStripStepOperator

/-!
# The step operator commutes with a convergent series

Summing the recursion that defines the clock iterates requires the step operator to pass through the
sum. It is linear, so this is the term-by-term differentiation of the previous file together with
the elementary behaviour of a sum under multiplication by a fixed value and division by a constant.

The summability of the second derivatives is Cauchy's estimate applied to the summable bound on the
functions themselves.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Set Complex Metric

/-- **The step operator commutes with a series of holomorphic functions.** -/
theorem clockStripStep_tsum {ρ₂ ρ₁ ρ' : ℝ} (h21 : ρ₂ < ρ₁) (h1ρ : ρ₁ < ρ')
    {V : ℂ → ℂ} {f : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ} {M : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ m, DifferentiableOn ℂ (f m) (imStrip ρ'))
    (hM : ∀ m, ∀ w ∈ imStrip ρ', ‖f m w‖ ≤ M m) (hMs : Summable M)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ imStrip ρ₂) :
    clockStripStep V (fun w => ∑' m, f m w) z = ∑' m, clockStripStep V (f m) z := by
  have h2ρ : ρ₂ < ρ' := lt_trans h21 h1ρ
  have hgap : (0 : ℝ) < ρ' - ρ₂ := by linarith
  have hz' : z ∈ imStrip ρ' := imStrip_mono h2ρ.le hz
  -- summability of the second derivatives, by Cauchy's estimate
  have hsum1 : Summable fun m => deriv (deriv (f m)) z := by
    refine Summable.of_norm_bounded
      (g := fun m => 16 * M m / (ρ' - ρ₂) ^ 2) ?_ fun m => ?_
    · simpa [mul_div_assoc] using (hMs.mul_left 16).div_const ((ρ' - ρ₂) ^ 2)
    · exact norm_deriv_deriv_le_on_imStrip h2ρ (hf m) (hM m) (le_of_lt (mem_imStrip.mp hz))
  have hsumf : Summable fun m => f m z :=
    Summable.of_norm_bounded hMs fun m => hM m z hz'
  have hsum2 : Summable fun m => V z * f m z := hsumf.mul_left _
  have hlhs : clockStripStep V (fun w => ∑' m, f m w) z
      = (deriv (deriv fun w => ∑' m, f m w) z + V z * ∑' m, f m z) / 4 := rfl
  have hrhs : ∀ m, clockStripStep V (f m) z = (deriv (deriv (f m)) z + V z * f m z) / 4 :=
    fun m => rfl
  rw [hlhs, deriv_deriv_tsum_of_holomorphic h21 h1ρ hf hM hMs hz, ← tsum_mul_left,
    ← hsum1.tsum_add hsum2, ← tsum_div_const]
  exact tsum_congr fun m => (hrhs m).symm

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

# Finite Signed Even Frequency Atoms Are Not Markov

- **ID:** finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / source-transfer guardrail
- **Grade:** BRIDGE / guardrail. Door-2 reduces the proof to finite
  exponential-sum dominance, so this is not a native theorem. Its use is to
  exclude a false source-transfer shape.
- **Source:** `positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md`;
  `source-selector-repair-obligation-ledger.md`;
  `seam-log-markov-pick-rh-equivalence.md`
- **Statement:** A nonzero finite signed sum of real FE-even exponential
  frequency germs cannot produce a Markov/Stieltjes moment sequence in the
  seam-square coordinate. Its shifted moments are negative on infinitely many
  indices.

## Setup

Let `n>=1`, and let

`0 < lambda_1 < ... < lambda_n`

and let `c_1,...,c_n` be real coefficients with `c_n != 0`. Equal frequencies
are first combined, so the displayed top coefficient is nonzero. Define

`L(z)=sum_{j=1}^n c_j (cosh(lambda_j sqrt(z))-1)`.

For `k>=1`, define the shifted seam moments

`T_k=-2k(-1)^k [z^k]L(z)`.

Set `x_j=lambda_j^2`.

## Theorem

If the signed frequency sum is nonzero, then there are infinitely many `k` for
which

`T_k < 0`.

Consequently `(T_k)_{k>=1}` is not the moment sequence of a positive Borel
measure on `R_+`. In particular, the finite signed real FE-even frequency atom
span intersects the Markov/Stieltjes target only at zero.

## Proof

The coefficient calculation gives

`[z^k]L(z)=sum_{j=1}^n c_j lambda_j^(2k)/(2k)!`

and hence

`T_k = (-1)^(k+1) (sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j^k)/(2k-1)!`.

Let

`S_k=sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j^k`.

Since `0 < x_1 < ... < x_n`,

`S_k / x_n^k = c_n + sum_{j<n} c_j (x_j/x_n)^k -> c_n`.

Thus, for all sufficiently large `k`, `S_k` has the sign of `c_n`.

If `c_n>0`, then for every sufficiently large even `k`,

`T_k = - S_k/(2k-1)! < 0`.

If `c_n<0`, then for every sufficiently large odd `k`,

`T_k = S_k/(2k-1)! < 0`.

In either case infinitely many shifted moments are negative. Since every moment
of a positive measure on `R_+` is nonnegative, no positive Markov/Stieltjes
representation exists.

## Consequence For Signed Counterterm Routes

`positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md` ruled out positive summation over
FE-even real frequencies. This theorem rules out the finite signed atomic
escape as well. A signed correction made from finitely many real FE-even
frequency atoms cannot repair the Markov target; the dominant frequency forces
tail sign oscillation.

Therefore a completed source proof cannot be a finite signed real-frequency
counterterm patched onto the positive cone. Any viable signed correction must
be genuinely outside this finite atom class: an infinite/nonlocal source object,
an archimedean-prime interaction, a multiplicative correlation identity, or a
closed boundary/index construction.

## Boundary

This theorem does not rule out infinite signed distributions with no largest
frequency, complex or imaginary frequencies, non-frequency source terms, or the
completed explicit formula. It only closes the finite real atom model.

## Theatre Test

For any proposed signed counterterm proof of seam-log Markov positivity:

1. Does the proof reduce the completed correction to finitely many real FE-even
   frequency atoms?
2. If yes, combine equal frequencies and inspect the top nonzero frequency.
3. The top frequency fixes the sign of `S_k` for large `k`, so `T_k` is negative
   on one tail parity.
4. Which source mechanism prevents that dominance argument from applying?

## Novelty Status

The proof is elementary finite exponential-sum dominance. The significant part
is the route audit: signed finite atom corrections are not the missing
completed interaction.

# Chronological chord capacity: computational leads

Exploratory numerical work, 2026-09-05. Results are not proof certificates. Scripts ran on the authorized Runpod (`157.157.221.29:27094`, directory `/root/chronological-chord-capacity`), with 24 Python workers and one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker. Environment: 32 available CPUs, NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1. Source and result JSON files are retained here.

## Question and method

For a pairing D of ordered endpoints, put `P_D(d)=∏_(i,j in D) Σ_(i≤k<j) d_k`, with variation budget `Σ|d_k|=1`.

`search.py` tested all 121 nonzero ternary coefficient vectors up to overall sign in the five-dimensional noncrossing basis on six endpoints. Each of 32 seeds sampled 72,000 positive and 72,000 signed Dirichlet increment vectors (concentration 0.3). Twelve coefficient vectors with the strongest apparent signed advantage received constrained SLSQP refinement, with analytic gradients, all 16 sign patterns modulo overall sign, and both objective signs. Output: `results.json`.

`basis_probe.py` tested the stronger conjecture `Σ_D |P_D(d)|/cap(D) ≤ 1`, for all noncrossing pairings on 4–12 endpoints. Individual-diagram capacities were supplied by a recursive interval-product formula using rational arithmetic; that implementation is part of the exploratory model, not a formal certificate. For each chord count, six seeds and both sign classes used 2,500 Dirichlet samples and SLSQP refinement from the 12 strongest samples. Output: `basis-results.json`.

## Outcomes

The first experiment found no resolved advantage from signed probe motion. This finite search establishes no equality theorem, and the full signed-versus-monotone question remains open.

The normalized-basis conjecture failed decisively from three chords onward. Best numerical values, rounded:

| Chords | Observed maximum |
|---|---:|
| 2 | 1.000000 |
| 3 | 1.132006 |
| 4 | 1.410792 |
| 5 | 1.896740 |
| 6 | 2.690254 |

These are local numerical optima, not certified global maxima. Signed sampling did not improve the best monotone value at reported precision. Small errors above 1 in degree two are floating-point effects.

## Exact mathematical consequence

The three-chord result suggested the two-term combination `27D+R`, where `D=(01)(23)(45)` and `R=(05)(14)(23)`. At gaps `(1/3,0,1/3,0,1/3)`, cost is exactly 1 and response exactly `10/9`, disproving the proposed bound without numerical inputs.

Independent symbolic reasoning then gave the global optimum: `q=(50-√313)/81` and `K=27q(1-q)²/4+q²`. Gaps `((1-q)/2,0,q,0,(1-q)/2)` attain K. Triangle inequalities, endpoint AM–GM, and a factored cubic optimality gap prove the upper bound for every signed gap vector. This exact argument is checked in `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/ChronologicalTensor/SixPoint.lean`; no JSON data or optimizer output enters Lean.

Further reasoning resolved the existence of signed advantage outside the first experiment's ternary coefficient class: `27D-R` has monotone capacity exactly 1, while gaps `(1/3,0,-1/3,0,1/3)` give `-28/27`. This is checked independently in `ChronologicalTensor/Reversal.lean`. It is not an output of either search.

Useful next questions concern composition across independent blocks and how nesting suppresses reversal-sensitive response. The degree 4–6 numerical values remain leads only.

# Signed prime recursion and changing arithmetic alignment

**Status:** two empirical hunches falsified; exact signed cofactor transport and a divisor information audit formalized. No new all-scale cancellation bound and no RH proof. Numerical results are exploratory, despite this folder's pipeline location.

Positivity is suspended as the proposed producer in this investigation. This is a research constraint, not a theorem that all positive or spectral methods fail. Corpus starting points, frozen predictions, controls, and adaptive decisions are in [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md).

## What the algebraic audit establishes

The actual observable is exactly

`R(N)=-sum(n<=N) lambda(n) w(n) - N sum(n<=N) lambda(n)/n`,

where `w(n)=sum(p prime dividing n) log p` counts each distinct prime divisor once. Expanding theta and reindexing the finite product region proves this: complete multiplicativity and the prime value -1 give `lambda(m)=-lambda(pm)`.

`LiouvillePrimeErrorDivisorAudit.lean` proves both the theta-pairing collapse and the full error identity, unconditionally and without computational premises. Scratch/direct checks and the named leaf build pass; both axiom audits contain only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The alignment observable therefore re-expresses weighted Liouville cancellation; it does not supply a second independent arithmetic constraint. A representation may still expose a useful estimate, but that estimate has not been found.

The cyclic-shift controls break complete multiplicativity. Their ranks discriminate from the chosen coarse-data controls, but cannot establish a mechanism beyond the multiplicative identity they destroy. The generic signed dilation theorem also holds for every ratio kernel, so that theorem alone does not distinguish the literal counting-error kernel. **Further alignment scans are paused.** A new experimental target must state a source-specific property or estimate, distinguish it from these identities, and specify controls that retain the properties it claims to use.

## What changed our understanding

The literal arithmetic does not consistently make the measured prime-counting error smaller. Relative to interventions preserving every dyadic cofactor block's sign count and signed sum, it can strongly suppress or strongly amplify the same error pairing. The reversal involves many cofactor scales and survives removing the smallest cofactors. An apparent doubling law mostly extends to other primes, but has decisive failures.

These observations reject a fixed direction of improvement for this observable. They do not yet identify a replacement asymptotic law. The exact residue specifies what a signed dilation argument must control instead of assuming reversal.

## Experiment 1: keep both discarded remainders

For a completely multiplicative sign function f and S(N)=sum(n<=N) f(n), the corpus's exact log recursion gives

`S(N) log N = P(N) + Elog(N) + Epp(N)`,

where P is the signed prime sum, Elog is the log-weight replacement error, and Epp is the complete contribution from higher prime powers. The existing general bounds on the two errors are O(N), inadequate for an RH producer.

At all **37** literal Liouville cutoffs from 4096 through 2097152, Elog and Epp have the same sign. At the last cutoff their values divided by sqrt(N) are approximately **-1.34944** and **-2.75630**. Their addition provides no saving. Four of seven random completely multiplicative controls also reinforce at every tested cutoff; the other three sometimes cancel. Thus the two discarded errors do not exhibit a distinctive hidden cancellation in this sample. See `results.json`.

# Perfect-pairing enclosure depth: numerical leads

**Outcome:** no validated numerical counterexample was found to depth-one stabilization in degrees three or four, or to depth-two stabilization in degree four. This finite search proves none of those universal statements. The known cubic reversal form has independently proved exact depth one; other coefficient combinations remain open.

## Question and method

For each noncrossing perfect pairing D on 2d ordered endpoints, form its gap polynomial `P_D=∏_(i,j∈D) Σ_(i≤q<j) g_q`. These give 5 generators in degree three and 14 in degree four. We searched coefficient combinations P for a signed variation-one probe with `|S^k P(g)|` greater than the monotone capacity, where S is total displacement.

The search ran on the authorized Runpod, in `/root/chronological-chord-capacity`, using 24 independent worker processes. Degree/depth pairs were (3,1), (4,1), and (4,2), with eight deterministic seeds each. BLAS/OpenMP environment variables were set to one thread before importing NumPy. SciPy 1.10.1 and NumPy 1.24.4 were used. The additional HiGHS `threads` option emitted `Unknown solver options: threads`; do not interpret the JSON's `library_threads` field as a measured backend thread count. The environment caps and 24-process pool are explicit in the source. The warning filter was broadened after the run to suppress this repeated diagnostic; numerical code is unchanged.

For each seed:

- A simplex grid plus 800 random monotone probes supplied 1,801 initial constraints in degree three or 2,516 in degree four.
- Linear programming selected coefficients against 40 signed target probes. Columns were scaled by their sampled maxima for conditioning.
- The best three candidates underwent at most ten rounds of monotone constraint exchange and optimization inside the signed probe's orthant, using analytic gradients and SLSQP.
- A first normalization check used 20,000 fresh monotone probes and local optimization.
- A separate validation used another 30,000 monotone probes per candidate, plus both the previously found monotone witness and the absolute value of the purported signed witness as optimization starts.

All 24 jobs completed. Three individual LP calls failed and were handled without treating their outputs as candidates. The search and validation are heuristic global searches; both can miss optima.

# Signed recursion: discovery protocol

Status: exploratory measurements, not an RH proof. Positivity is suspended as a proposed producer in this investigation. This is a research allocation, not a no-go theorem about all positivity methods.

## Source evidence and question

`Sieve/MultiplicativeLogRecursion.lean` preserves the exact signed prime recursion but bounds two remainders by O(N). `LiouvilleDirichletSeries.sum_divisors_liouvilleC` identifies the exact square-supported divisor convolution. The frontier and universal ledgers reject generic energy positivity as a substitute for source-specific cancellation. These three corpus observations motivate inspecting the discarded signed terms before replacing their bounds.

For a real completely multiplicative sign function f, put S(N)=sum(n<=N) f(n), and define

- Elog(N)=sum(n<=N) f(n) log(N/n);
- Eeven(N)=sum(p^k<=N, k>=2 even) log(p) f(p)^k S(floor(N/p^k));
- Eodd(N)=sum(p^k<=N, k>=3 odd) log(p) f(p)^k S(floor(N/p^k));
- P(N)=sum(p<=N) log(p) f(p) S(floor(N/p)).

The exact identity is S(N) log(N)=P(N)+Elog(N)+Eeven(N)+Eodd(N). No absolute value is taken before this addition.

Discovery question: are the two discarded errors individually small, or do they need cancellation against one another? Is their signed relationship specific to literal f(p)=-1, or also present in independent random completely multiplicative controls?

No primary conjecture is frozen before observing data. This is hypothesis-generating work. Any subsequent claim must be frozen separately and attacked on new cutoffs/seeds. In particular, bounded finite normalized values will not be called an asymptotic theorem.

## Design and falsifiers

Use the literal Liouville function, seven seeded random prime-sign controls, and f=1 as an implementation and degeneracy control. Every control preserves complete multiplicativity, so the exact recursion remains applicable. The all-one control is not an experiment on cancellation; its predictable behavior checks the measurement implementation.

Measure powers of two and three intervening cutoffs per octave from 4096 through 2097152. Record all signed terms, square-root and square-root-times-log normalizations, sign disagreements, the fraction of absolute remainder size retained after summing, and the exact-recursion residual. These are linear/signed diagnostics, not quadratic energies or PSD tests.

Reconstruct signs independently by smallest-prime-factor recursion on a short prefix. Validate the prime-power identity against the weighted sum. A failed identity check invalidates the batch. Do not infer RH from finite bounds or from random-control similarity.

Run only on the authorized Runpod, at most eight worker processes, one numerical-library thread per worker, and a 120-second command cap. Download scripts and results. No numerical output enters a Lean proof.
